frameworks.name: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5
frameworks.description: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) SP 800-53 Rev. 5 provides a standardized approach for assessing, monitoring and authorizing cloud computing products and services to manage information security risk. These policies address a subset of NIST SP 800-53 R5 controls. Additional policies will be added in upcoming releases. For more information, visit https://aka.ms/nist800-53r5-initiative

frameworks.name: FedRAMP High
frameworks.description: FedRAMP is a US government-wide program that provides a standardized approach to security assessment, authorization, and continuous monitoring for cloud-based products and services. FedRAMP defines a set of controls for Low, Moderate, or High security impact level systems based on NIST baseline controls. These policies address a subset of FedRAMP (High) controls. For more information, visit https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/compliance/offerings/offering-fedramp

frameworks.name: FedRAMP Moderate
frameworks.description: FedRAMP is a U.S. government-wide program that provides a standardized approach to security assessment, authorization, and continuous monitoring for cloud-based products and services. FedRAMP defines a set of controls for Low, Moderate, or High security impact level systems based on NIST baseline controls. These policies address a subset of FedRAMP (Moderate) controls. Additional policies will be added in upcoming releases. For more information, visit https://www.fedramp.gov/documents-templates/

frameworks.name: NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2
frameworks.description: The US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) promotes and maintains measurement standards and guidelines to help protect the information and information systems of federal agencies. In response to Executive Order 13556 on managing controlled unclassified information (CUI), it published NIST SP 800-171. These policies address a subset of NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 controls. For more information, visit https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/compliance/offerings/offering-nist-800-171

frameworks.name: CMMC 2.0 Level 2
frameworks.description: This initiative includes policies that address a subset of CMMC 2.0 Level 2 practices. Additional policies will be added in upcoming releases. For more information, visit https://aka.ms/cmmc2l2-initiative.

frameworks.name: FBI Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) v5.9.5
frameworks.description: Standards by the FBI to secure criminal justice information, covering data access, transmission, and storage.

frameworks.name: NIST CSF v2.0
frameworks.description: Risk-based approach to managing cybersecurity threats, offering guidance for improving cybersecurity practices.

frameworks.name: Microsoft cloud security benchmark
frameworks.description: The Microsoft cloud security benchmark initiative represents the policies and controls implementing security recommendations defined in Microsoft cloud security benchmark, see https://aka.ms/azsecbm. This also serves as the Microsoft Defender for Cloud default policy initiative. You can directly assign this initiative, or manage its policies and compliance results within Microsoft Defender for Cloud.

frameworks.name: CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark v2.0.0
frameworks.description: The Center for Internet Security (CIS) is a nonprofit entity whose mission is to 'identify, develop, validate, promote, and sustain best practice solutions for cyberdefense.' CIS benchmarks are configuration baselines and best practices for securely configuring a system. These policies address a subset of CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark v2.0.0 controls. For more information, visit https://aka.ms/cisazure200-initiative

frameworks.name: CIS Azure Foundations v3.0.0
frameworks.description: CIS Azure Foundations 3.0 defines benchmark controls to improve cloud security in Microsoft Azure. The standard aligns with industry best practices for risk reduction and secure configurations.

frameworks.name: ISO/IEC 27001 2022
frameworks.description: International standard for managing information security via an Information Security Management System (ISMS).

frameworks.name: SOC 2 Type 2
frameworks.description: A System and Organization Controls (SOC) 2 is a report based on the Trust Service Principles and Criteria established by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA). The Report evaluates an organization's information system relevant to the following principles: security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality and privacy. These policies address a subset of SOC 2 Type 2 controls. For more information, visit https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/compliance/offerings/offering-soc-2

frameworks.name: PCI DSS v4.0.1
frameworks.description: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard, focusing on protecting credit card transaction data.

frameworks.name: HITRUST/HIPAA
frameworks.description: Health Information Trust Alliance (HITRUST) helps organizations from all sectors-but especially healthcare-effectively manage data, information risk, and compliance. HITRUST certification means that the organization has undergone a thorough assessment of the information security program. These policies address a subset of HITRUST controls. For more information, visit https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/governance/policy/samples/hipaa-hitrust-9-2

frameworks.name: EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) 2016/679
frameworks.description: Comprehensive data protection law regulating personal data processing within the EU.

frameworks.name: EU 2022/2555 (NIS2) 2022
frameworks.description: Enhances cybersecurity across the EU with security measures and incident reporting for critical sectors.

sovereignty-global.name: Sovereignty Baseline - Global Policies
sovereignty-global.description: The Microsoft Cloud for Sovereignty recommends global policies to help organizations achieve their sovereignty goals by default denying the creation of resources outside of approved regions. More details can be found here: https://aka.ms/SovereigntyBaselinePolicies

sovereignty-confidential.name: Sovereignty Baseline - Confidential Policies
sovereignty-confidential.description: The Microsoft Cloud for Sovereignty recommends confidential policies to help organizations achieve their sovereignty goals by default denying the creation of resources outside of approved regions, denying resources that are not backed by Azure Confidential Computing, and denying data storage resources that are not using Customer-Managed Keys. More details can be found here: https://aka.ms/SovereigntyBaselinePolicies

r: Managed disks should be double encrypted with both platform-managed and customer-managed keys
Both operating systems and data disks in Azure Kubernetes Service clusters should be encrypted by customer-managed keys
SQL servers should use customer-managed keys to encrypt data at rest
Azure Container Instance container group should use customer-managed key for encryption
OS and data disks should be encrypted with a customer-managed key

roles.name: Application-Owners
roles.description: Contributor role granted for application/operations team at resource group level

roles.name: Network-Management
roles.description: Platform-wide global connectivity management: virtual networks, UDRs, NSGs, NVAs, VPN, Azure ExpressRoute, and others

roles.name: Network-Subnet-Contributor
roles.description: Enterprise-scale custom Role Definition. Grants full access to manage Virtual Network subnets, but no other network resources.

roles.name: Security-Operations
roles.description: Security Administrator role with a horizontal view across the entire Azure estate and the Azure Key Vault purge policy.

roles.name: Subscription-Owner
roles.description: Delegated role for subscription owner generated from subscription Owner role

Audit-AppGW-WAF.displayName: Web Application Firewall (WAF) should be enabled for Application Gateway
Audit-AppGW-WAF.description: Assign the WAF should be enabled for Application Gateway audit policy.
Audit-AppGW-WAF.definitionName: Web Application Firewall (WAF) should be enabled for Application Gateway

Audit-PeDnsZones.displayName: Audit Private Link Private DNS Zone resources
Audit-PeDnsZones.description: Audits the deployment of Private Link Private DNS Zone resources in the Corp landing zone.
Audit-PeDnsZones.definitionName: Audit or Deny the creation of Private Link Private DNS Zones

Audit-ResourceRGLocation.displayName: Resource Group and Resource locations should match
Audit-ResourceRGLocation.description: Resource Group and Resource locations should match.
Audit-ResourceRGLocation.definitionName: Audit resource location matches resource group location

Audit-TrustedLaunch.displayName: Audit virtual machines for Trusted Launch support
Audit-TrustedLaunch.description: Trusted Launch improves security of a Virtual Machine which requires VM SKU, OS Disk & OS Image to support it (Gen 2). To learn more about Trusted Launch, visit https://aka.ms/trustedlaunch.
Audit-TrustedLaunch.definitionName: Audit virtual machines for Trusted Launch support

Audit-UnusedResources.displayName: Unused resources driving cost should be avoided
Audit-UnusedResources.description: This Policy initiative is a group of Policy definitions that help optimize cost by detecting unused but chargeable resources. Leverage this Policy initiative as a cost control to reveal orphaned resources that are driving cost.
Audit-UnusedResources.definitionName: Unused resources driving cost should be avoided

Deny-Classic-Resources.displayName: Deny the deployment of classic resources
Deny-Classic-Resources.description: Denies deployment of classic resource types under the assigned scope.

Deny-HybridNetworking.displayName: Deny the deployment of vWAN/ER/VPN gateway resources
Deny-HybridNetworking.description: Denies deployment of vWAN/ER/VPN gateway resources in the Corp landing zone.

Deny-IP-forwarding.displayName: Network interfaces should disable IP forwarding
Deny-IP-forwarding.description: This policy denies the network interfaces which enabled IP forwarding. The setting of IP forwarding disables Azure's check of the source and destination for a network interface. This should be reviewed by the network security team.
Deny-IP-forwarding.definitionName: Network interfaces should disable IP forwarding

Deny-MgmtPorts-Internet.displayName: Management port access from the Internet should be blocked
Deny-MgmtPorts-Internet.description: This policy denies any network security rule that allows management port access from the Internet
Deny-MgmtPorts-Internet.definitionName: Management port access from the Internet should be blocked

Deny-Priv-Esc-AKS.displayName: Kubernetes clusters should not allow container privilege escalation
Deny-Priv-Esc-AKS.description: Do not allow containers to run with privilege escalation to root in a Kubernetes cluster. This recommendation is part of CIS 5.2.5 which is intended to improve the security of your Kubernetes environments. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for AKS Engine and Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.
Deny-Priv-Esc-AKS.definitionName: Kubernetes clusters should not allow container privilege escalation

Deny-Privileged-AKS.displayName: Kubernetes cluster should not allow privileged containers
Deny-Privileged-AKS.description: Do not allow privileged containers creation in a Kubernetes cluster. This recommendation is part of CIS 5.2.1 which is intended to improve the security of your Kubernetes environments. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for AKS Engine and Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.
Deny-Privileged-AKS.definitionName: Kubernetes cluster should not allow privileged containers

Deny-Public-Endpoints.displayName: Public network access should be disabled for PaaS services
Deny-Public-Endpoints.description: This policy initiative is a group of policies that prevents creation of Azure PaaS services with exposed public endpoints
Deny-Public-Endpoints.definitionName: Public network access should be disabled for PaaS services

Deny-Public-IP.displayName: Deny the creation of public IP
Deny-Public-IP.description: This policy denies creation of Public IPs under the assigned scope.

Deny-Public-IP-On-NIC.displayName: Deny network interfaces having a public IP associated
Deny-Public-IP-On-NIC.description: This policy denies network interfaces from having a public IP associated to it under the assigned scope.
Deny-Public-IP-On-NIC.definitionName: Network interfaces should not have public IPs

Deny-Storage-http.displayName: Secure transfer to storage accounts should be enabled
Deny-Storage-http.description: Audit requirement of Secure transfer in your storage account. Secure transfer is an option that forces your storage account to accept requests only from secure connections (HTTPS). Use of HTTPS ensures authentication between the server and the service and protects data in transit from network layer attacks such as man-in-the-middle, eavesdropping, and session-hijacking
Deny-Storage-http.definitionName: Secure transfer to storage accounts should be enabled

Deny-Subnet-Without-Nsg.displayName: Subnets should have a Network Security Group
Deny-Subnet-Without-Nsg.description: This policy denies the creation of a subnet without a Network Security Group to protect traffic across subnets.
Deny-Subnet-Without-Nsg.definitionName: Subnets should have a Network Security Group

Deny-UnmanagedDisk.displayName: Deny virtual machines and virtual machine scale sets that do not use managed disk
Deny-UnmanagedDisk.description: Deny virtual machines that do not use managed disk. It checks the managed disk property on virtual machine OS Disk fields.
Deny-UnmanagedDisk.definitionName: Audit VMs that do not use managed disks

DenyAction-DeleteUAMIAMA.displayName: Do not allow deletion of the User Assigned Managed Identity used by AMA
DenyAction-DeleteUAMIAMA.description: This policy provides a safeguard against accidental removal of the User Assigned Managed Identity used by AMA by blocking delete calls using deny action effect.
DenyAction-DeleteUAMIAMA.definitionName: Do not allow deletion of specified resource and resource type

Deploy-ASC-Monitoring.description: Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark policy initiative.

Deploy-AzActivity-Log.displayName: Configure Azure Activity logs to stream to specified Log Analytics workspace
Deploy-AzActivity-Log.description: Deploys the diagnostic settings for Azure Activity to stream subscriptions audit logs to a Log Analytics workspace to monitor subscription-level events
Deploy-AzActivity-Log.definitionName: Configure Azure Activity logs to stream to specified Log Analytics workspace

Deploy-AzSqlDb-Auditing.displayName: Configure SQL servers to have auditing enabled to Log Analytics workspace
Deploy-AzSqlDb-Auditing.description: To ensure the operations performed against your SQL assets are captured, SQL servers should have auditing enabled. If auditing is not enabled, this policy will configure auditing events to flow to the specified Log Analytics workspace.
Deploy-AzSqlDb-Auditing.definitionName: Configure SQL servers to have auditing enabled to Log Analytics workspace

Deploy-Diag-LogsCat.displayName: Enable category group resource logging for supported resources to Log Analytics
Deploy-Diag-LogsCat.description: Resource logs should be enabled to track activities and events that take place on your resources and give you visibility and insights into any changes that occur. This initiative deploys diagnostic setting using the allLogs category group to route logs to an Event Hub for all supported resources.
Deploy-Diag-LogsCat.definitionName: Enable audit category group resource logging for supported resources to Log Analytics

Deploy-GuestAttest.displayName: Configure prerequisites to enable Guest Attestation on Trusted Launch enabled VMs
Deploy-GuestAttest.description: Configure the Trusted Launch enabled virtual machines to automatically install the Guest Attestation extension and enable system-assigned managed identity to allow Azure Security Center to proactively attest and monitor the boot integrity. Boot integrity is attested via Remote Attestation. For more details, please refer to the following link - https://aka.ms/trustedlaunch.
Deploy-GuestAttest.definitionName: [Preview]: Configure prerequisites to enable Guest Attestation on Trusted Launch enabled VMs

Deploy-MCSB2-Monitoring.description: Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark v2 policy initiative.

Deploy-MDEndpoints.displayName: [Preview]: Deploy Microsoft Defender for Endpoint agent
Deploy-MDEndpoints.description: Deploy Microsoft Defender for Endpoint agent on applicable images.
Deploy-MDEndpoints.definitionName: [Preview]: Deploy Microsoft Defender for Endpoint agent

Deploy-MDEndpointsAMA.displayName: Configure multiple Microsoft Defender for Endpoint integration settings with Microsoft Defender for Cloud
Deploy-MDEndpointsAMA.description: Configure the multiple Microsoft Defender for Endpoint integration settings with Microsoft Defender for Cloud (WDATP, WDATP_EXCLUDE_LINUX_PUBLIC_PREVIEW, WDATP_UNIFIED_SOLUTION etc.). See: https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/defender-for-cloud/integration-defender-for-endpoint for more information.
Deploy-MDEndpointsAMA.definitionName: Configure multiple Microsoft Defender for Endpoint integration settings with Microsoft Defender for Cloud

Deploy-MDFC-Config-H224.displayName: Deploy Microsoft Defender for Cloud configuration
Deploy-MDFC-Config-H224.description: Deploy Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Security Contacts
Deploy-MDFC-Config-H224.definitionName: Deploy Microsoft Defender for Cloud configuration

Deploy-MDFC-DefSQL-AMA.displayName: Enable Defender for SQL on SQL VMs and Arc-enabled SQL Servers
Deploy-MDFC-DefSQL-AMA.description: Microsoft Defender for SQL collects events from the agents and uses them to provide security alerts and tailored hardening tasks (recommendations).
Deploy-MDFC-DefSQL-AMA.definitionName: Configure SQL VMs and Arc-enabled SQL Servers to install Microsoft Defender for SQL and AMA with a user-defined LA workspace

Deploy-MDFC-OssDb.displayName: Configure Advanced Threat Protection to be enabled on open-source relational databases
Deploy-MDFC-OssDb.description: Enable Advanced Threat Protection on your non-Basic tier open-source relational databases to detect anomalous activities indicating unusual and potentially harmful attempts to access or exploit databases. See https://aka.ms/AzDforOpenSourceDBsDocu.
Deploy-MDFC-OssDb.definitionName: Configure Advanced Threat Protection to be enabled on open-source relational databases

Deploy-MDFC-SqlAtp.displayName: Configure Azure Defender to be enabled on SQL Servers and SQL Managed Instances
Deploy-MDFC-SqlAtp.description: Enable Azure Defender on your SQL Servers and SQL Managed Instances to detect anomalous activities indicating unusual and potentially harmful attempts to access or exploit databases.
Deploy-MDFC-SqlAtp.definitionName: Configure Azure Defender to be enabled on SQL Servers and SQL Managed Instances

Deploy-Private-DNS-Zones.displayName: Configure Azure PaaS services to use private DNS zones
Deploy-Private-DNS-Zones.description: This policy initiative is a group of policies that ensures private endpoints to Azure PaaS services are integrated with Azure Private DNS zones
Deploy-Private-DNS-Zones.definitionName: Configure Azure PaaS services to use private DNS zones

Deploy-SQL-TDE.description: This policy ensures that Transparent Data Encryption is enabled on SQL Servers.
Deploy-SQL-TDE.definitionName: Deploy SQL DB transparent data encryption

Deploy-SQL-Threat.displayName: Deploy Threat Detection on SQL servers
Deploy-SQL-Threat.description: This policy ensures that Threat Detection is enabled on SQL Servers.
Deploy-SQL-Threat.definitionName: Configure Azure Defender to be enabled on SQL servers

Deploy-SvcHealth-BuiltIn.displayName: Configure subscriptions to enable service health alert monitoring rule
Deploy-SvcHealth-BuiltIn.description: Assignable at the subscription or management group level, this policy ensures that each subscription has a service health alert rule configured with alert conditions and mapping to action groups as specified in the policy parameters. By default creates a resource group, alert rule and action group configured to send emails to subscription owners for all service health events.
Deploy-SvcHealth-BuiltIn.definitionName: Configure subscriptions to enable service health alert monitoring rule

Deploy-VM-Backup.displayName: Configure backup on virtual machines without a given tag to a new recovery services vault with a default policy
Deploy-VM-Backup.description: Enforce backup for all virtual machines by deploying a recovery services vault in the same location and resource group as the virtual machine. Doing this is useful when different application teams in your organization are allocated separate resource groups and need to manage their own backups and restores. You can optionally exclude virtual machines containing a specified tag to control the scope of assignment. See https://aka.ms/AzureVMAppCentricBackupExcludeTag.
Deploy-VM-Backup.definitionName: Configure backup on virtual machines without a given tag to a new recovery services vault with a default policy

Deploy-VM-ChangeTrack.displayName: Enable ChangeTracking and Inventory for virtual machines
Deploy-VM-ChangeTrack.description: Enable ChangeTracking and Inventory for virtual machines. Takes Data Collection Rule ID as parameter and asks for an option to input applicable locations and user-assigned identity for Azure Monitor Agent.
Deploy-VM-ChangeTrack.definitionName: Enable ChangeTracking and Inventory for virtual machines

Deploy-VM-Monitoring.description: Enable Azure Monitor for the virtual machines (VMs) in the specified scope (management group, subscription or resource group). Takes Log Analytics workspace as parameter.
Deploy-VM-Monitoring.definitionName: Enable Azure Monitor for VMs with Azure Monitoring Agent(AMA)

Deploy-VMSS-ChangeTrack.displayName: Enable ChangeTracking and Inventory for virtual machine scale sets
Deploy-VMSS-ChangeTrack.description: Enable ChangeTracking and Inventory for virtual machine scale sets. Takes Data Collection Rule ID as parameter and asks for an option to input applicable locations and user-assigned identity for Azure Monitor Agent.
Deploy-VMSS-ChangeTrack.definitionName: Enable ChangeTracking and Inventory for virtual machine scale sets

Deploy-VMSS-Monitoring.displayName: Enable Azure Monitor for Virtual Machine Scale Sets
Deploy-VMSS-Monitoring.description: Enable Azure Monitor for the Virtual Machine Scale Sets in the specified scope (Management group, Subscription or resource group). Takes Log Analytics workspace as parameter. Note: if your scale set upgradePolicy is set to Manual, you need to apply the extension to the all VMs in the set by calling upgrade on them. In CLI this would be az vmss update-instances.
Deploy-VMSS-Monitoring.definitionName: Enable Azure Monitor for VMSS with Azure Monitoring Agent(AMA)

Deploy-vmArc-ChangeTrack.displayName: Enable ChangeTracking and Inventory for Arc-enabled virtual machines
Deploy-vmArc-ChangeTrack.description: Enable ChangeTracking and Inventory for Arc-enabled virtual machines. Takes Data Collection Rule ID as parameter and asks for an option to input applicable locations.
Deploy-vmArc-ChangeTrack.definitionName: Enable ChangeTracking and Inventory for Arc-enabled virtual machines

Deploy-vmHybr-Monitoring.displayName: Enable Azure Monitor for Hybrid Virtual Machines
Deploy-vmHybr-Monitoring.description: Enable Azure Monitor for Hybrid Virtual Machines in the specified scope (Management group, Subscription or resource group).
Deploy-vmHybr-Monitoring.definitionName: Enable Azure Monitor for Hybrid VMs with AMA

Enable-AUM-CheckUpdates.displayName: Configure periodic checking for missing system updates on azure virtual machines and Arc-enabled virtual machines.
Enable-AUM-CheckUpdates.description: Configure auto-assessment (every 24 hours) for OS updates. You can control the scope of assignment according to machine subscription, resource group, location or tag. Learn more about this for Windows: https://aka.ms/computevm-windowspatchassessmentmode, for Linux: https://aka.ms/computevm-linuxpatchassessmentmode.
Enable-AUM-CheckUpdates.definitionName: Configure periodic checking for missing system updates on azure virtual machines and Arc-enabled virtual machines

Enable-DDoS-VNET.displayName: Virtual networks should be protected by Azure DDoS Network Protection
Enable-DDoS-VNET.description: Protect your virtual networks against volumetric and protocol attacks with Azure DDoS Network Protection. For more information, visit https://aka.ms/ddosprotectiondocs.
Enable-DDoS-VNET.definitionName: Virtual networks should be protected by Azure DDoS Protection

Enforce-ACSB.displayName: Enforce Azure Compute Security Baseline compliance auditing
Enforce-ACSB.description: This initiative assignment enables Azure Compute Security Baseline compliance auditing for Windows and Linux virtual machines.
Enforce-ACSB.definitionName: Enforce Azure Compute Security Benchmark compliance auditing

Enforce-AKS-HTTPS.displayName: Kubernetes clusters should be accessible only over HTTPS
Enforce-AKS-HTTPS.description: Use of HTTPS ensures authentication and protects data in transit from network layer eavesdropping attacks. This capability is currently generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and in preview for AKS Engine and Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more info, visit https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc
Enforce-AKS-HTTPS.definitionName: Kubernetes clusters should be accessible only over HTTPS

72650e9f-97bc-4b2a-ab5f-9781a9fcecbc.n: Windows machines should meet requirements of the Azure compute security baseline
72650e9f-97bc-4b2a-ab5f-9781a9fcecbc.d: Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol. Machines are non-compliant if the machine is not configured correctly for one of the recommendations in the Azure compute security baseline.

fc9b3da7-8347-4380-8e70-0a0361d8dedd.n: Linux machines should meet requirements for the Azure compute security baseline
fc9b3da7-8347-4380-8e70-0a0361d8dedd.d: Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol. Machines are non-compliant if the machine is not configured correctly for one of the recommendations in the Azure compute security baseline.

bed48b13-6647-468e-aa2f-1af1d3f4dd40.n: Windows Defender Exploit Guard should be enabled on your machines
bed48b13-6647-468e-aa2f-1af1d3f4dd40.d: Windows Defender Exploit Guard uses the Azure Policy Guest Configuration agent. Exploit Guard has four components that are designed to lock down devices against a wide variety of attack vectors and block behaviors commonly used in malware attacks while enabling enterprises to balance their security risk and productivity requirements (Windows only).

e6955644-301c-44b5-a4c4-528577de6861.n: Audit Linux machines that do not have the passwd file permissions set to 0644
e6955644-301c-44b5-a4c4-528577de6861.d: Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol. Machines are non-compliant if Linux machines that do not have the passwd file permissions set to 0644

5b054a0d-39e2-4d53-bea3-9734cad2c69b.n: Audit Windows machines that allow re-use of the passwords after the specified number of unique passwords
5b054a0d-39e2-4d53-bea3-9734cad2c69b.d: Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol. Machines are non-compliant if Windows machines that allow re-use of the passwords after the specified number of unique passwords. Default value for unique passwords is 24

da0f98fe-a24b-4ad5-af69-bd0400233661.n: Audit Windows machines that do not store passwords using reversible encryption
da0f98fe-a24b-4ad5-af69-bd0400233661.d: Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol. Machines are non-compliant if Windows machines that do not store passwords using reversible encryption

4ceb8dc2-559c-478b-a15b-733fbf1e3738.n: Audit Windows machines that do not have the maximum password age set to specified number of days
4ceb8dc2-559c-478b-a15b-733fbf1e3738.d: Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol. Machines are non-compliant if Windows machines that do not have the maximum password age set to specified number of days. Default value for maximum password age is 70 days

5752e6d6-1206-46d8-8ab1-ecc2f71a8112.n: Windows machines should be configured to use secure communication protocols
5752e6d6-1206-46d8-8ab1-ecc2f71a8112.d: To protect the privacy of information communicated over the Internet, your machines should use the latest version of the industry-standard cryptographic protocol, Transport Layer Security (TLS). TLS secures communications over a network by encrypting a connection between machines.

630c64f9-8b6b-4c64-b511-6544ceff6fd6.n: Authentication to Linux machines should require SSH keys
630c64f9-8b6b-4c64-b511-6544ceff6fd6.d: Although SSH itself provides an encrypted connection, using passwords with SSH still leaves the VM vulnerable to brute-force attacks. The most secure option for authenticating to an Azure Linux virtual machine over SSH is with a public-private key pair, also known as SSH keys. Learn more: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-machines/linux/create-ssh-keys-detailed.

237b38db-ca4d-4259-9e47-7882441ca2c0.n: Audit Windows machines that do not have the minimum password age set to specified number of days
237b38db-ca4d-4259-9e47-7882441ca2c0.d: Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol. a2d0e922-65d0-40c4-8f87-ea6da2d307a2.n: Audit Windows machines that do not restrict the minimum password length to specified number of characters

febd0533-8e55-448f-b837-bd0e06f16469.n: Kubernetes cluster containers should only use allowed images
febd0533-8e55-448f-b837-bd0e06f16469.d: Use images from trusted registries to reduce the Kubernetes cluster's exposure risk to unknown vulnerabilities, security issues and malicious images. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

95edb821-ddaf-4404-9732-666045e056b4.n: Kubernetes cluster should not allow privileged containers
95edb821-ddaf-4404-9732-666045e056b4.d: Do not allow privileged containers creation in a Kubernetes cluster. This recommendation is part of CIS 5.2.1 which is intended to improve the security of your Kubernetes environments. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

233a2a17-77ca-4fb1-9b6b-69223d272a44.n: Kubernetes cluster services should listen only on allowed ports
233a2a17-77ca-4fb1-9b6b-69223d272a44.d: Restrict services to listen only on allowed ports to secure access to the Kubernetes cluster. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

e345eecc-fa47-480f-9e88-67dcc122b164.n: Kubernetes cluster containers CPU and memory resource limits should not exceed the specified limits
e345eecc-fa47-480f-9e88-67dcc122b164.d: Enforce container CPU and memory resource limits to prevent resource exhaustion attacks in a Kubernetes cluster. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

f06ddb64-5fa3-4b77-b166-acb36f7f6042.n: Kubernetes cluster pods and containers should only run with approved user and group IDs
f06ddb64-5fa3-4b77-b166-acb36f7f6042.d: Control the user, primary group, supplemental group and file system group IDs that pods and containers can use to run in a Kubernetes Cluster. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

1c6e92c9-99f0-4e55-9cf2-0c234dc48f99.n: Kubernetes clusters should not allow container privilege escalation
1c6e92c9-99f0-4e55-9cf2-0c234dc48f99.d: Do not allow containers to run with privilege escalation to root in a Kubernetes cluster. This recommendation is part of CIS 5.2.5 which is intended to improve the security of your Kubernetes environments. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

47a1ee2f-2a2a-4576-bf2a-e0e36709c2b8.n: Kubernetes cluster containers should not share host namespaces
47a1ee2f-2a2a-4576-bf2a-e0e36709c2b8.d: Block pod containers from sharing the host process ID namespace, host IPC namespace, and host network namespace in a Kubernetes cluster. This recommendation aligns with the Kubernetes Pod Security Standards for host namespaces and is part of CIS 5.2.1, 5.2.2 and 5.2.3 which are intended to improve the security of your Kubernetes environments. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Servi

df49d893-a74c-421d-bc95-c663042e5b80.n: Kubernetes cluster containers should run with a read only root file system
df49d893-a74c-421d-bc95-c663042e5b80.d: Run containers with a read only root file system to protect from changes at run-time with malicious binaries being added to PATH in a Kubernetes cluster. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

1a5b4dca-0b6f-4cf5-907c-56316bc1bf3d.n: Kubernetes clusters should be accessible only over HTTPS
1a5b4dca-0b6f-4cf5-907c-56316bc1bf3d.d: Use of HTTPS ensures authentication and protects data in transit from network layer eavesdropping attacks. This capability is currently generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and in preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more info, visit https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc

c26596ff-4d70-4e6a-9a30-c2506bd2f80c.n: Kubernetes cluster containers should only use allowed capabilities
c26596ff-4d70-4e6a-9a30-c2506bd2f80c.d: Restrict the capabilities to reduce the attack surface of containers in a Kubernetes cluster. This recommendation is part of CIS 5.2.8 and CIS 5.2.9 which are intended to improve the security of your Kubernetes environments. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

511f5417-5d12-434d-ab2e-816901e72a5e.n: Kubernetes cluster containers should only use allowed AppArmor profiles
511f5417-5d12-434d-ab2e-816901e72a5e.d: Containers should only use allowed AppArmor profiles in a Kubernetes cluster. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

82985f06-dc18-4a48-bc1c-b9f4f0098cfe.n: Kubernetes cluster pods should only use approved host network and port list
82985f06-dc18-4a48-bc1c-b9f4f0098cfe.d: Restrict pod access to the host network and the allowable host ports in a Kubernetes cluster. This recommendation is part of CIS 5.2.4 which is intended to improve the security of your Kubernetes environments and aligns with Pod Security Standards (PSS) for hostPorts. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information

098fc59e-46c7-4d99-9b16-64990e543d75.n: Kubernetes cluster pod hostPath volumes should only use allowed host paths
098fc59e-46c7-4d99-9b16-64990e543d75.d: Limit pod HostPath volume mounts to the allowed host paths in a Kubernetes Cluster. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

a6fb4358-5bf4-4ad7-ba82-2cd2f41ce5e9.n: Auditing on SQL server should be enabled
a6fb4358-5bf4-4ad7-ba82-2cd2f41ce5e9.d: Auditing on your SQL Server should be enabled to track database activities across all databases on the server and save them in an audit log.

ef619a2c-cc4d-4d03-b2ba-8c94a834d85b.n: API Management services should use a virtual network
ef619a2c-cc4d-4d03-b2ba-8c94a834d85b.d: Azure Virtual Network deployment provides enhanced security, isolation and allows you to place your API Management service in a non-internet routable network that you control access to. These networks can then be connected to your on-premises networks using various VPN technologies, which enables access to your backend services within the network and/or on-premises. 71ef260a-8f18-47b7-abcb-62d0673d94dc.n: Azure AI Services resources should have key access disabled (disable local authentication)
71ef260a-8f18-47b7-abcb-62d0673d94dc.d: Key access (local authentication) is recommended to be disabled for security. Azure OpenAI Studio, typically used in development/testing, requires key access and will not function if key access is disabled. After disabling, Microsoft Entra ID becomes the only access method, which allows maintaining minimum privilege principle and granular control. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/AI/auth

055aa869-bc98-4af8-bafc-23f1ab6ffe2c.d: Deploy Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) in front of public facing web applications for additional inspection of incoming traffic. Web Application Firewall (WAF) provides centralized protection of your web applications from common exploits and vulnerabilities such as SQL injections, Cross-Site Scripting, local and remote file executions. 564feb30-bf6a-4854-b4bb-0d2d2d1e6c66.n: Web Application Firewall (WAF) should be enabled for Application Gateway
564feb30-bf6a-4854-b4bb-0d2d2d1e6c66.d: Deploy Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) in front of public facing web applications for additional inspection of incoming traffic. 862e97cf-49fc-4a5c-9de4-40d4e2e7c8eb.n: Azure Cosmos DB accounts should have firewall rules
862e97cf-49fc-4a5c-9de4-40d4e2e7c8eb.d: Firewall rules should be defined on your Azure Cosmos DB accounts to prevent traffic from unauthorized sources. Accounts that have at least one IP rule defined with the virtual network filter enabled are deemed compliant. Accounts disabling public access are also deemed compliant.

d9da03a1-f3c3-412a-9709-947156872263.n: Azure HDInsight clusters should use encryption in transit to encrypt communication between Azure HDInsight cluster nodes
d9da03a1-f3c3-412a-9709-947156872263.d: Data can be tampered with during transmission between Azure HDInsight cluster nodes. Enabling encryption in transit addresses problems of misuse and tampering during this transmission.

617c02be-7f02-4efd-8836-3180d47b6c68.n: Service Fabric clusters should have the ClusterProtectionLevel property set to EncryptAndSign
617c02be-7f02-4efd-8836-3180d47b6c68.d: Service Fabric provides three levels of protection (None, Sign and EncryptAndSign) for node-to-node communication using a primary cluster certificate. Set the protection level to ensure that all node-to-node messages are encrypted and digitally signed

c43e4a30-77cb-48ab-a4dd-93f175c63b57.n: Microsoft Antimalware for Azure should be configured to automatically update protection signatures
c43e4a30-77cb-48ab-a4dd-93f175c63b57.d: This policy audits any Windows virtual machine not configured with automatic update of Microsoft Antimalware protection signatures.

35de8462-03ff-45b3-5746-9d4603c74c56.d: CMA_C1751 - Implement an insider threat program

d93fe1be-13e4-421d-9c21-3158e2fa2667.n: Implement plans of action and milestones for security program process
