12430be1-6cc8-4527-a9a8-e3d38f250096.n: Web Application Firewall (WAF) should use the specified mode for Application Gateway
12430be1-6cc8-4527-a9a8-e3d38f250096.d: Mandates the use of 'Detection' or 'Prevention' mode to be active on all Web Application Firewall policies for Application Gateway.

5e1de0e3-42cb-4ebc-a86d-61d0c619ca48.n: Public network access should be disabled for PostgreSQL flexible servers
5e1de0e3-42cb-4ebc-a86d-61d0c619ca48.d: Disabling the public network access property improves security by ensuring your Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible servers can only be accessed from a private endpoint. This configuration strictly disables access from any public address space outside of Azure IP range and denies all logins that match IP based firewall rules.

82067dbb-e53b-4e06-b631-546d197452d9.n: Keys using RSA cryptography should have a specified minimum key size
82067dbb-e53b-4e06-b631-546d197452d9.d: Set the minimum allowed key size for use with your key vaults. Use of RSA keys with small key sizes is not a secure practice and doesn't meet many industry certification requirements.

75c4f823-d65c-4f29-a733-01d0077fdbcb.n: Keys should be the specified cryptographic type RSA or EC
75c4f823-d65c-4f29-a733-01d0077fdbcb.d: Some applications require the use of keys backed by a specific cryptographic type. Enforce a particular cryptographic key type, RSA or EC, in your environment.

c251913d-7d24-4958-af87-478ed3b9ba41.n: Flow logs should be configured for every network security group
c251913d-7d24-4958-af87-478ed3b9ba41.d: Audit for network security groups to verify if flow logs are configured. Enabling flow logs allows to log information about IP traffic flowing through network security group. It can be used for optimizing network flows, monitoring throughput, verifying compliance, detecting intrusions and more.

425bea59-a659-4cbb-8d31-34499bd030b8.n: Web Application Firewall (WAF) should use the specified mode for Azure Front Door Service
425bea59-a659-4cbb-8d31-34499bd030b8.d: Mandates the use of 'Detection' or 'Prevention' mode to be active on all Web Application Firewall policies for Azure Front Door Service.

c9299215-ae47-4f50-9c54-8a392f68a052.n: Public network access should be disabled for MySQL flexible servers
c9299215-ae47-4f50-9c54-8a392f68a052.d: Disabling the public network access property improves security by ensuring your Azure Database for MySQL flexible servers can only be accessed from a private endpoint. This configuration strictly disables access from any public address space outside of Azure IP range and denies all logins that match IP or virtual network-based firewall rules.

cee51871-e572-4576-855c-047c820360f0.n: Certificates using RSA cryptography should have the specified minimum key size
cee51871-e572-4576-855c-047c820360f0.d: Manage your organizational compliance requirements by specifying a minimum key size for RSA certificates stored in your key vault.

ff25f3c8-b739-4538-9d07-3d6d25cfb255.n: Keys using elliptic curve cryptography should have the specified curve names
ff25f3c8-b739-4538-9d07-3d6d25cfb255.d: Keys backed by elliptic curve cryptography can have different curve names. Some applications are only compatible with specific elliptic curve keys. Enforce the types of elliptic curve keys that are allowed to be created in your environment.

f655e522-adff-494d-95c2-52d4f6d56a42.n: Guest Attestation extension should be installed on supported Windows virtual machines scale sets
f655e522-adff-494d-95c2-52d4f6d56a42.d: Install Guest Attestation extension on supported virtual machines scale sets to allow Azure Security Center to proactively attest and monitor the boot integrity. Once installed, boot integrity will be attested via Remote Attestation. This assessment applies to Trusted Launch and Confidential Windows virtual machine scale sets.

40e85574-ef33-47e8-a854-7a65c7500560.n: Azure MySQL flexible server should have Microsoft Entra Only Authentication enabled
40e85574-ef33-47e8-a854-7a65c7500560.d: Disabling local authentication methods and allowing only Microsoft Entra Authentication improves security by ensuring that Azure MySQL flexible server can exclusively be accessed by Microsoft Entra identities.

3b980d31-7904-4bb7-8575-5665739a8052.n: An activity log alert should exist for specific Security operations
3b980d31-7904-4bb7-8575-5665739a8052.d: This policy audits specific Security operations with no activity log alerts configured.

6b2122c1-8120-4ff5-801b-17625a355590.n: Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes clusters should have the Azure Policy extension installed
6b2122c1-8120-4ff5-801b-17625a355590.d: The Azure Policy extension for Azure Arc provides at-scale enforcements and safeguards on your Arc enabled Kubernetes clusters in a centralized, consistent manner. Learn more at https://aka.ms/akspolicydoc.

a1817ec0-a368-432a-8057-8371e17ac6ee.n: All authorization rules except RootManageSharedAccessKey should be removed from Service Bus namespace
a1817ec0-a368-432a-8057-8371e17ac6ee.d: Service Bus clients should not use a namespace level access policy that provides access to all queues and topics in a namespace. To align with the least privilege security model, you should create access policies at the entity level for queues and topics to provide access to only the specific entity

a2a5b911-5617-447e-a49e-59dbe0e0434b.n: Resource logs in Azure Key Vault Managed HSM should be enabled
a2a5b911-5617-447e-a49e-59dbe0e0434b.d: To recreate activity trails for investigation purposes when a security incident occurs or when your network is compromised, you may want to audit by enabling resource logs on Managed HSMs. Please follow the instructions here: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/key-vault/managed-hsm/logging.

7804b5c7-01dc-4723-969b-ae300cc07ff1.n: Azure Machine Learning Computes should be in a virtual network
7804b5c7-01dc-4723-969b-ae300cc07ff1.d: Azure Virtual Networks provide enhanced security and isolation for your Azure Machine Learning Compute Clusters and Instances, as well as subnets, access control policies, and other features to further restrict access. When a compute is configured with a virtual network, it is not publicly addressable and can only be accessed from virtual machines and applications within the virtual network.

a1181c5f-672a-477a-979a-7d58aa086233.n: Security Center standard pricing tier should be selected
a1181c5f-672a-477a-979a-7d58aa086233.d: The standard pricing tier enables threat detection for networks and virtual machines, providing threat intelligence, anomaly detection, and behavior analytics in Azure Security Center

3e596b57-105f-48a6-be97-03e9243bad6e.n: Azure Monitor solution 'Security and Audit' must be deployed
3e596b57-105f-48a6-be97-03e9243bad6e.d: This policy ensures that Security and Audit is deployed.

3dc5edcd-002d-444c-b216-e123bbfa37c0.n: Windows virtual machines should enable Azure Disk Encryption or EncryptionAtHost.
3dc5edcd-002d-444c-b216-e123bbfa37c0.d: Although a virtual machine's OS and data disks are encrypted-at-rest by default using platform managed keys, resource disks (temp disks), data caches, and data flowing between Compute and Storage resources are not encrypted. Use Azure Disk Encryption or EncryptionAtHost to remediate. Visit https://aka.ms/diskencryptioncomparison to compare encryption offerings. This policy requires two prerequisit

8af8f826-edcb-4178-b35f-851ea6fea615.n: Azure Container Instance container group should deploy into a virtual network
8af8f826-edcb-4178-b35f-851ea6fea615.d: Secure communication between your containers with Azure Virtual Networks. When you specify a virtual network, resources within the virtual network can securely and privately communicate with each other.

7ff426e2-515f-405a-91c8-4f2333442eb5.n: SQL Auditing settings should have Action-Groups configured to capture critical activities
7ff426e2-515f-405a-91c8-4f2333442eb5.d: The AuditActionsAndGroups property should contain at least SUCCESSFUL_DATABASE_AUTHENTICATION_GROUP, FAILED_DATABASE_AUTHENTICATION_GROUP, BATCH_COMPLETED_GROUP to ensure a thorough audit logging

5450f5bd-9c72-4390-a9c4-a7aba4edfdd2.n: Cosmos DB database accounts should have local authentication methods disabled
5450f5bd-9c72-4390-a9c4-a7aba4edfdd2.d: Disabling local authentication methods improves security by ensuring that Cosmos DB database accounts exclusively require Azure Active Directory identities for authentication. Learn more at: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/cosmos-db/how-to-setup-rbac#disable-local-auth.

33936777-f2ac-45aa-82ec-07958ec9ade4.n: Windows machines should meet requirements for 'Security Options - Audit'
33936777-f2ac-45aa-82ec-07958ec9ade4.d: Windows machines should have the specified Group Policy settings in the category 'Security Options - Audit' for forcing audit policy subcategory and shutting down if unable to log security audits. This policy requires that the Guest Configuration prerequisites have been deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol.

3ac7c827-eea2-4bde-acc7-9568cd320efa.n: Machines should have secret findings resolved
3ac7c827-eea2-4bde-acc7-9568cd320efa.d: Audits virtual machines to detect whether they contain secret findings from the secret scanning solutions on your virtual machines.

0fdf0491-d080-4575-b627-ad0e843cba0f.n: Public network access should be disabled for Container registries
0fdf0491-d080-4575-b627-ad0e843cba0f.d: Disabling public network access improves security by ensuring that container registries are not exposed on the public internet. Creating private endpoints can limit exposure of container registry resources. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/acr/portal/public-network and https://aka.ms/acr/private-link.

afe0c3be-ba3b-4544-ba52-0c99672a8ad6.n: Resource logs in Azure Machine Learning Workspaces should be enabled
afe0c3be-ba3b-4544-ba52-0c99672a8ad6.d: Resource logs enable recreating activity trails to use for investigation purposes when a security incident occurs or when your network is compromised.

87845465-c458-45f3-af66-dcd62176f397.n: Windows machines should meet requirements for 'System Audit Policies - Privilege Use'
87845465-c458-45f3-af66-dcd62176f397.d: Windows machines should have the specified Group Policy settings in the category 'System Audit Policies - Privilege Use' for auditing nonsensitive and other privilege use. This policy requires that the Guest Configuration prerequisites have been deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol.

f71be03e-e25b-4d0f-b8bc-9b3e309b66c0.n: Windows machines should meet requirements for 'Security Options - Recovery console'
f71be03e-e25b-4d0f-b8bc-9b3e309b66c0.d: Windows machines should have the specified Group Policy settings in the category 'Security Options - Recovery console' for allowing floppy copy and access to all drives and folders. This policy requires that the Guest Configuration prerequisites have been deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol.

1a4e592a-6a6e-44a5-9814-e36264ca96e7.n: Azure Monitor log profile should collect logs for categories 'write;' 'delete;' and 'action'
1a4e592a-6a6e-44a5-9814-e36264ca96e7.d: This policy ensures that a log profile collects logs for categories 'write;' 'delete;' and 'action'

423dd1ba-798e-40e4-9c4d-b6902674b423.n: Kubernetes clusters should disable automounting API credentials
423dd1ba-798e-40e4-9c4d-b6902674b423.d: Disable automounting API credentials to prevent a potentially compromised Pod resource to run API commands against Kubernetes clusters. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

2158ddbe-fefa-408e-b43f-d4faef8ff3b8.n: Synapse Workspaces should use only Microsoft Entra identities for authentication during workspace creation
2158ddbe-fefa-408e-b43f-d4faef8ff3b8.d: Require Synapse Workspaces to be created with Microsoft Entra-only authentication. This policy doesn't block local authentication from being re-enabled on resources after create. Consider using the 'Microsoft Entra-only authentication' initiative instead to require both. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/Synapse.

797b37f7-06b8-444c-b1ad-fc62867f335a.n: Azure Cosmos DB should disable public network access
797b37f7-06b8-444c-b1ad-fc62867f335a.d: Disabling public network access improves security by ensuring that your CosmosDB account isn't exposed on the public internet. Creating private endpoints can limit exposure of your CosmosDB account. Learn more at: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/cosmos-db/how-to-configure-private-endpoints#blocking-public-network-access-during-account-creation.

0a914e76-4921-4c19-b460-a2d36003525a.n: Audit resource location matches resource group location
0a914e76-4921-4c19-b460-a2d36003525a.d: Audit that the resource location matches its resource group location

94d9aca8-3757-46df-aa51-f218c5f11954.n: Windows machines should meet requirements for 'System Audit Policies - Account Management'
94d9aca8-3757-46df-aa51-f218c5f11954.d: Windows machines should have the specified Group Policy settings in the category 'System Audit Policies - Account Management' for auditing application, security, and user group management, and other management events. This policy requires that the Guest Configuration prerequisites have been deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol.

8c6a50c6-9ffd-4ae7-986f-5fa6111f9a54.n: Storage accounts should prevent shared key access
8c6a50c6-9ffd-4ae7-986f-5fa6111f9a54.d: Audit requirement of Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) to authorize requests for your storage account. By default, requests can be authorized with either Azure Active Directory credentials, or by using the account access key for Shared Key authorization. Of these two types of authorization, Azure AD provides superior security and ease of use over Shared Key, and is recommended by Microsoft.

2d21331d-a4c2-4def-a9ad-ee4e1e023beb.n: App Service apps should use a virtual network service endpoint
2d21331d-a4c2-4def-a9ad-ee4e1e023beb.d: Use virtual network service endpoints to restrict access to your app from selected subnets from an Azure virtual network. To learn more about App Service service endpoints, visit https://aka.ms/appservice-vnet-service-endpoint.

3d2a3320-2a72-4c67-ac5f-caa40fbee2b2.n: Audit Windows machines that have extra accounts in the Administrators group
3d2a3320-2a72-4c67-ac5f-caa40fbee2b2.d: Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol. Machines are non-compliant if the local Administrators group contains members that are not listed in the policy parameter.

46aa9b05-0e60-4eae-a88b-1e9d374fa515.n: Cognitive Services accounts should use customer owned storage
46aa9b05-0e60-4eae-a88b-1e9d374fa515.d: Use customer owned storage to control the data stored at rest in Cognitive Services. To learn more about customer owned storage, visit https://aka.ms/cogsvc-cmk.

3bc8a0d5-38e0-4a3d-a657-2cb64468fc34.n: Azure Defender for SQL should be enabled for unprotected MySQL flexible servers
3bc8a0d5-38e0-4a3d-a657-2cb64468fc34.d: Audit MySQL flexible servers without Advanced Data Security

f4826e5f-6a27-407c-ae3e-9582eb39891d.n: Authorization rules on the Event Hub instance should be defined
f4826e5f-6a27-407c-ae3e-9582eb39891d.d: Audit existence of authorization rules on Event Hub entities to grant least-privileged access

3d9f5e4c-9947-4579-9539-2a7695fbc187.n: App Configuration should disable public network access
3d9f5e4c-9947-4579-9539-2a7695fbc187.d: Disabling public network access improves security by ensuring that the resource isn't exposed on the public internet. You can limit exposure of your resources by creating private endpoints instead. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/appconfig/private-endpoint.

009a0c92-f5b4-4776-9b66-4ed2b4775563.n: Private endpoint connections on Batch accounts should be enabled
009a0c92-f5b4-4776-9b66-4ed2b4775563.d: Private endpoint connections allow secure communication by enabling private connectivity to Batch accounts without a need for public IP addresses at the source or destination. Learn more about private endpoints in Batch at https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/batch/private-connectivity.

67e010c1-640d-438e-a3a5-feaccb533a98.n: Windows machines should meet requirements for 'Administrative Templates - Network'
67e010c1-640d-438e-a3a5-feaccb533a98.d: Windows machines should have the specified Group Policy settings in the category 'Administrative Templates - Network' for guest logons, simultaneous connections, network bridge, ICS, and multicast name resolution. This policy requires that the Guest Configuration prerequisites have been deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol.

967a4b4b-2da9-43c1-b7d0-f98d0d74d0b1.n: App Configuration should use a customer-managed key
967a4b4b-2da9-43c1-b7d0-f98d0d74d0b1.d: Customer-managed keys provide enhanced data protection by allowing you to manage your encryption keys. This is often required to meet compliance requirements.

e96a9a5f-07ca-471b-9bc5-6a0f33cbd68f.n: Azure Machine Learning Computes should have local authentication methods disabled
e96a9a5f-07ca-471b-9bc5-6a0f33cbd68f.d: Disabling local authentication methods improves security by ensuring that Machine Learning Computes require Azure Active Directory identities exclusively for authentication. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/azure-ml-aad-policy.

c4857be7-912a-4c75-87e6-e30292bcdf78.n: [Preview]: Container Registry should use a virtual network service endpoint
c4857be7-912a-4c75-87e6-e30292bcdf78.d: This policy audits any Container Registry not configured to use a virtual network service endpoint.

ae5d2f14-d830-42b6-9899-df6cfe9c71a3.n: SQL Server should use a virtual network service endpoint
ae5d2f14-d830-42b6-9899-df6cfe9c71a3.d: This policy audits any SQL Server not configured to use a virtual network service endpoint.

a1840de2-8088-4ea8-b153-b4c723e9cb01.n: Azure Kubernetes Service clusters should have Defender profile enabled
a1840de2-8088-4ea8-b153-b4c723e9cb01.d: Microsoft Defender for Containers provides cloud-native Kubernetes security capabilities including environment hardening, workload protection, and run-time protection. When you enable the SecurityProfile.AzureDefender on your Azure Kubernetes Service cluster, an agent is deployed to your cluster to collect security event data. Learn more about Microsoft Defender for Containers in https://docs.micr

fa498b91-8a7e-4710-9578-da944c68d1fe.n: [Preview]: Azure PostgreSQL flexible server should have Microsoft Entra Only Authentication enabled
fa498b91-8a7e-4710-9578-da944c68d1fe.d: Disabling local authentication methods and allowing only Microsoft Entra Authentication improves security by ensuring that Azure PostgreSQL flexible server can exclusively be accessed by Microsoft Entra identities.

7796937f-307b-4598-941c-67d3a05ebfe7.n: Azure subscriptions should have a log profile for Activity Log
7796937f-307b-4598-941c-67d3a05ebfe7.d: This policy ensures if a log profile is enabled for exporting activity logs. It audits if there is no log profile created to export the logs either to a storage account or to an event hub.

4c3c6c5f-0d47-4402-99b8-aa543dd8bcee.n: Audit flow logs configuration for every virtual network
4c3c6c5f-0d47-4402-99b8-aa543dd8bcee.d: Audit for virtual network to verify if flow logs are configured. Enabling flow logs allows to log information about IP traffic flowing through virtual network. It can be used for optimizing network flows, monitoring throughput, verifying compliance, detecting intrusions and more.

d6759c02-b87f-42b7-892e-71b3f471d782.n: Azure AI Services resources should use Azure Private Link
d6759c02-b87f-42b7-892e-71b3f471d782.d: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The Private Link platform reduces data leakage risks by handling the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. Learn more about private links at: https://aka.ms/AzurePrivateLink/Overview

e068b215-0026-4354-b347-8fb2766f73a2.n: Windows machines should meet requirements for 'User Rights Assignment'
e068b215-0026-4354-b347-8fb2766f73a2.d: Windows machines should have the specified Group Policy settings in the category 'User Rights Assignment' for allowing log on locally, RDP, access from the network, and many other user activities. This policy requires that the Guest Configuration prerequisites have been deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol.

97566dd7-78ae-4997-8b36-1c7bfe0d8121.n: Secure Boot should be enabled on supported Windows virtual machines
97566dd7-78ae-4997-8b36-1c7bfe0d8121.d: Enable Secure Boot on supported Windows virtual machines to mitigate against malicious and unauthorized changes to the boot chain. Once enabled, only trusted bootloaders, kernel and kernel drivers will be allowed to run. This assessment applies to Trusted Launch and Confidential Windows virtual machines.

c9d007d0-c057-4772-b18c-01e546713bcd.n: Storage accounts should allow access from trusted Microsoft services
c9d007d0-c057-4772-b18c-01e546713bcd.d: Some Microsoft services that interact with storage accounts operate from networks that can't be granted access through network rules. To help this type of service work as intended, allow the set of trusted Microsoft services to bypass the network rules. These services will then use strong authentication to access the storage account.

2a7a701e-dff3-4da9-9ec5-42cb98594c0b.n: Windows machines should meet requirements for 'System Audit Policies - Policy Change'
2a7a701e-dff3-4da9-9ec5-42cb98594c0b.d: Windows machines should have the specified Group Policy settings in the category 'System Audit Policies - Policy Change' for auditing changes to system audit policies. This policy requires that the Guest Configuration prerequisites have been deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol.

492a29ed-d143-4f03-b6a4-705ce081b463.n: Windows machines should meet requirements for 'Security Options - User Account Control'
492a29ed-d143-4f03-b6a4-705ce081b463.d: Windows machines should have the specified Group Policy settings in the category 'Security Options - User Account Control' for mode for admins, behavior of elevation prompt, and virtualizing file and registry write failures. This policy requires that the Guest Configuration prerequisites have been deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol.

35d9882c-993d-44e6-87d2-db66ce21b636.n: Windows machines should meet requirements for 'Windows Firewall Properties'
35d9882c-993d-44e6-87d2-db66ce21b636.d: Windows machines should have the specified Group Policy settings in the category 'Windows Firewall Properties' for firewall state, connections, rule management, and notifications. This policy requires that the Guest Configuration prerequisites have been deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol.

60d21c4f-21a3-4d94-85f4-b924e6aeeda4.n: Storage Accounts should use a virtual network service endpoint
60d21c4f-21a3-4d94-85f4-b924e6aeeda4.d: This policy audits any Storage Account not configured to use a virtual network service endpoint.

11e3da8c-1d68-4392-badd-0ff3c43ab5b0.n: [Preview]: Recovery Services vaults should use private link
11e3da8c-1d68-4392-badd-0ff3c43ab5b0.d: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The Private Link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. By mapping private endpoints to Azure Recovery Services vaults, data leakage risks are reduced. Learn more about private links for Azure Site Recover

adbe85b5-83e6-4350-ab58-bf3a4f736e5e.n: Microsoft Defender for Azure Cosmos DB should be enabled
adbe85b5-83e6-4350-ab58-bf3a4f736e5e.d: Microsoft Defender for Azure Cosmos DB is an Azure-native layer of security that detects attempts to exploit databases in your Azure Cosmos DB accounts Defender for Azure Cosmos DB detects potential SQL injections, known bad actors based on Microsoft Threat Intelligence, suspicious access patterns, and potential exploitations of your database through compromised identities or malicious insiders.

c39ba22d-4428-4149-b981-70acb31fc383.n: Azure Key Vault Managed HSM should have purge protection enabled
c39ba22d-4428-4149-b981-70acb31fc383.d: Malicious deletion of an Azure Key Vault Managed HSM can lead to permanent data loss. A malicious insider in your organization can potentially delete and purge Azure Key Vault Managed HSM. Purge protection protects you from insider attacks by enforcing a mandatory retention period for soft deleted Azure Key Vault Managed HSM. No one inside your organization or Microsoft will be able to purge your

e345b6c3-24bd-4c93-9bbb-7e5e49a17b78.n: Azure VPN gateways should not use 'basic' SKU
e345b6c3-24bd-4c93-9bbb-7e5e49a17b78.d: This policy ensures that VPN gateways do not use 'basic' SKU.

c75248c1-ea1d-4a9c-8fc9-29a6aabd5da8.n: Function apps should have authentication enabled
c75248c1-ea1d-4a9c-8fc9-29a6aabd5da8.d: Azure App Service Authentication is a feature that can prevent anonymous HTTP requests from reaching the Function app, or authenticate those that have tokens before they reach the Function app.

c5447c04-a4d7-4ba8-a263-c9ee321a6858.n: An activity log alert should exist for specific Policy operations
c5447c04-a4d7-4ba8-a263-c9ee321a6858.d: This policy audits specific Policy operations with no activity log alerts configured.

1c30f9cd-b84c-49cc-aa2c-9288447cc3b3.n: vTPM should be enabled on supported virtual machines
1c30f9cd-b84c-49cc-aa2c-9288447cc3b3.d: Enable virtual TPM device on supported virtual machines to facilitate Measured Boot and other OS security features that require a TPM. Once enabled, vTPM can be used to attest boot integrity. This assessment only applies to trusted launch enabled virtual machines.

1cb4d9c2-f88f-4069-bee0-dba239a57b09.n: Guest Attestation extension should be installed on supported Windows virtual machines
1cb4d9c2-f88f-4069-bee0-dba239a57b09.d: Install Guest Attestation extension on supported virtual machines to allow Azure Security Center to proactively attest and monitor the boot integrity. Once installed, boot integrity will be attested via Remote Attestation. This assessment applies to Trusted Launch and Confidential Windows virtual machines.

f2143251-70de-4e81-87a8-36cee5a2f29d.n: Windows machines should meet requirements for 'Security Settings - Account Policies'
f2143251-70de-4e81-87a8-36cee5a2f29d.d: Windows machines should have the specified Group Policy settings in the category 'Security Settings - Account Policies' for password history, age, length, complexity, and storing passwords using reversible encryption. This policy requires that the Guest Configuration prerequisites have been deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol.

146412e9-005c-472b-9e48-c87b72ac229e.n: A Microsoft Entra administrator should be provisioned for MySQL servers
146412e9-005c-472b-9e48-c87b72ac229e.d: Audit provisioning of a Microsoft Entra administrator for your MySQL server to enable Microsoft Entra authentication. Microsoft Entra authentication enables simplified permission management and centralized identity management of database users and other Microsoft services

32e6bbec-16b6-44c2-be37-c5b672d103cf.n: Azure SQL Database should be running TLS version 1.2 or newer
32e6bbec-16b6-44c2-be37-c5b672d103cf.d: Setting TLS version to 1.2 or newer improves security by ensuring your Azure SQL Database can only be accessed from clients using TLS 1.2 or newer. Using versions of TLS less than 1.2 is not recommended since they have well documented security vulnerabilities.

bd876905-5b84-4f73-ab2d-2e7a7c4568d9.n: Machines should be configured to periodically check for missing system updates
bd876905-5b84-4f73-ab2d-2e7a7c4568d9.d: To ensure periodic assessments for missing system updates are triggered automatically every 24 hours, the AssessmentMode property should be set to 'AutomaticByPlatform'. Learn more about AssessmentMode property for Windows: https://aka.ms/computevm-windowspatchassessmentmode, for Linux: https://aka.ms/computevm-linuxpatchassessmentmode.

8ac833bd-f505-48d5-887e-c993a1d3eea0.n: API endpoints in Azure API Management should be authenticated
8ac833bd-f505-48d5-887e-c993a1d3eea0.d: API endpoints published within Azure API Management should enforce authentication to help minimize security risk. Authentication mechanisms are sometimes implemented incorrectly or are missing. This allows attackers to exploit implementation flaws and to access data. Learn More about the OWASP API Threat for Broken User Authentication here: https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/api-management/mitigate

e15effd4-2278-4c65-a0da-4d6f6d1890e2.n: Log Analytics Workspaces should block non-Azure Active Directory based ingestion.
e15effd4-2278-4c65-a0da-4d6f6d1890e2.d: Enforcing log ingestion to require Azure Active Directory authentication prevents unauthenticated logs from an attacker which could lead to incorrect status, false alerts, and incorrect logs stored in the system.

7926a6d1-b268-4586-8197-e8ae90c877d7.n: Microsoft Defender for APIs should be enabled
7926a6d1-b268-4586-8197-e8ae90c877d7.d: Microsoft Defender for APIs brings new discovery, protection, detection, & response coverage to monitor for common API based attacks & security misconfigurations.

12d4fa5e-1f9f-4c21-97a9-b99b3c6611b5.n: Azure Key Vault should use RBAC permission model
12d4fa5e-1f9f-4c21-97a9-b99b3c6611b5.d: Enable RBAC permission model across Key Vaults. Learn more at: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/rbac-migration

a8793640-60f7-487c-b5c3-1d37215905c4.n: SQL Managed Instance should have the minimal TLS version of 1.2
a8793640-60f7-487c-b5c3-1d37215905c4.d: Setting minimal TLS version to 1.2 improves security by ensuring your SQL Managed Instance can only be accessed from clients using TLS 1.2. Using versions of TLS less than 1.2 is not recommended since they have well documented security vulnerabilities.

41388f1c-2db0-4c25-95b2-35d7f5ccbfa9.n: Azure Monitor should collect activity logs from all regions
41388f1c-2db0-4c25-95b2-35d7f5ccbfa9.d: This policy audits the Azure Monitor log profile which does not export activities from all Azure supported regions including global.

58383b73-94a9-4414-b382-4146eb02611b.n: Windows machines should meet requirements for 'System Audit Policies - Detailed Tracking'
58383b73-94a9-4414-b382-4146eb02611b.d: Windows machines should have the specified Group Policy settings in the category 'System Audit Policies - Detailed Tracking' for auditing DPAPI, process creation/termination, RPC events, and PNP activity. This policy requires that the Guest Configuration prerequisites have been deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol.

caf2d518-f029-4f6b-833b-d7081702f253.n: Windows machines should meet requirements for 'Security Options - Microsoft Network Server'
caf2d518-f029-4f6b-833b-d7081702f253.d: Windows machines should have the specified Group Policy settings in the category 'Security Options - Microsoft Network Server' for disabling SMB v1 server. This policy requires that the Guest Configuration prerequisites have been deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol.

06a78e20-9358-41c9-923c-fb736d382a4d.n: Audit VMs that do not use managed disks
06a78e20-9358-41c9-923c-fb736d382a4d.d: This policy audits VMs that do not use managed disks

d63edb4a-c612-454d-b47d-191a724fcbf0.n: Event Hub should use a virtual network service endpoint
d63edb4a-c612-454d-b47d-191a724fcbf0.d: This policy audits any Event Hub not configured to use a virtual network service endpoint.

9dfea752-dd46-4766-aed1-c355fa93fb91.n: Azure SQL Managed Instances should disable public network access
9dfea752-dd46-4766-aed1-c355fa93fb91.d: Disabling public network access (public endpoint) on Azure SQL Managed Instances improves security by ensuring that they can only be accessed from inside their virtual networks or via Private Endpoints. To learn more about public network access, visit https://aka.ms/mi-public-endpoint.

ca88aadc-6e2b-416c-9de2-5a0f01d1693f.n: Linux virtual machines should enable Azure Disk Encryption or EncryptionAtHost.
ca88aadc-6e2b-416c-9de2-5a0f01d1693f.d: Although a virtual machine's OS and data disks are encrypted-at-rest by default using platform managed keys, resource disks (temp disks), data caches, and data flowing between Compute and Storage resources are not encrypted. Use Azure Disk Encryption or EncryptionAtHost to remediate. Visit https://aka.ms/diskencryptioncomparison to compare encryption offerings. This policy requires two prerequisit

438c38d2-3772-465a-a9cc-7a6666a275ce.n: Azure Machine Learning Workspaces should disable public network access
438c38d2-3772-465a-a9cc-7a6666a275ce.d: Disabling public network access improves security by ensuring that the Machine Learning Workspaces aren't exposed on the public internet. You can control exposure of your workspaces by creating private endpoints instead. Learn more at: https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/machine-learning/how-to-configure-private-link?view=azureml-api-2&tabs=azure-portal.

95bccee9-a7f8-4bec-9ee9-62c3473701fc.n: App Service apps should have authentication enabled
95bccee9-a7f8-4bec-9ee9-62c3473701fc.d: Azure App Service Authentication is a feature that can prevent anonymous HTTP requests from reaching the web app, or authenticate those that have tokens before they reach the web app.

a21f8c92-9e22-4f09-b759-50500d1d2dda.n: Guest Attestation extension should be installed on supported Linux virtual machines scale sets
a21f8c92-9e22-4f09-b759-50500d1d2dda.d: Install Guest Attestation extension on supported Linux virtual machines scale sets to allow Azure Security Center to proactively attest and monitor the boot integrity. Once installed, boot integrity will be attested via Remote Attestation.  This assessment applies to Trusted Launch and Confidential Linux virtual machine scale sets.

d2e7ea85-6b44-4317-a0be-1b951587f626.n: Kubernetes clusters should not grant CAP_SYS_ADMIN security capabilities
d2e7ea85-6b44-4317-a0be-1b951587f626.d: To reduce the attack surface of your containers, restrict CAP_SYS_ADMIN Linux capabilities. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

13a6c84f-49a5-410a-b5df-5b880c3fe009.n: [Preview]: Linux virtual machines should use only signed and trusted boot components
13a6c84f-49a5-410a-b5df-5b880c3fe009.d: All OS boot components (boot loader, kernel, kernel drivers) must be signed by trusted publishers. Defender for Cloud has identified untrusted OS boot components on one or more of your Linux machines. To protect your machines from potentially malicious components, add them to your allow list or remove the identified components.

d31e5c31-63b2-4f12-887b-e49456834fa1.n: Microsoft Defender for SQL should be enabled for unprotected Synapse workspaces
d31e5c31-63b2-4f12-887b-e49456834fa1.d: Enable Defender for SQL to protect your Synapse workspaces. Defender for SQL monitors your Synapse SQL to detect anomalous activities indicating unusual and potentially harmful attempts to access or exploit databases.

b4dec045-250a-48c2-b5cc-e0c4eec8b5b4.n: A Microsoft Entra administrator should be provisioned for PostgreSQL servers
b4dec045-250a-48c2-b5cc-e0c4eec8b5b4.d: Audit provisioning of a Microsoft Entra administrator for your PostgreSQL server to enable Microsoft Entra authentication. Microsoft Entra authentication enables simplified permission management and centralized identity management of database users and other Microsoft services

0a9fbe0d-c5c4-4da8-87d8-f4fd77338835.n: Azure Defender for open-source relational databases should be enabled
0a9fbe0d-c5c4-4da8-87d8-f4fd77338835.d: Azure Defender for open-source relational databases detects anomalous activities indicating unusual and potentially harmful attempts to access or exploit databases. Learn more about the capabilities of Azure Defender for open-source relational databases at https://aka.ms/AzDforOpenSourceDBsDocu. Important: Enabling this plan will result in charges for protecting your open-source relational databas

d8cf8476-a2ec-4916-896e-992351803c44.n: Keys should have a rotation policy ensuring that their rotation is scheduled within the specified number of days after creation.
d8cf8476-a2ec-4916-896e-992351803c44.d: Manage your organizational compliance requirements by specifying the maximum number of days after key creation until it must be rotated.

b02aacc0-b073-424e-8298-42b22829ee0a.n: Activity log should be retained for at least one year
b02aacc0-b073-424e-8298-42b22829ee0a.d: This policy audits the activity log if the retention is not set for 365 days or forever (retention days set to 0).

245fc9df-fa96-4414-9a0b-3738c2f7341c.n: Resource logs in Azure Kubernetes Service should be enabled
245fc9df-fa96-4414-9a0b-3738c2f7341c.d: Azure Kubernetes Service's resource logs can help recreate activity trails when investigating security incidents. Enable it to make sure the logs will exist when needed

af99038c-02fd-4a2f-ac24-386b62bf32de.n: [Preview]: Machines should have ports closed that might expose attack vectors
af99038c-02fd-4a2f-ac24-386b62bf32de.d: Azure's Terms Of Use prohibit the use of Azure services in ways that could damage, disable, overburden, or impair any Microsoft server, or the network. The exposed ports identified by this recommendation need to be closed for your continued security. For each identified port, the recommendation also provides an explanation of the potential threat.

044985bb-afe1-42cd-8a36-9d5d42424537.n: Storage account keys should not be expired
044985bb-afe1-42cd-8a36-9d5d42424537.d: Ensure the user storage account keys are not expired when key expiration policy is set, for improving security of account keys by taking action when the keys are expired.

ea4d6841-2173-4317-9747-ff522a45120f.n: Key Vault should use a virtual network service endpoint
ea4d6841-2173-4317-9747-ff522a45120f.d: This policy audits any Key Vault not configured to use a virtual network service endpoint.

d38668f5-d155-42c7-ab3d-9b57b50f8fbf.n: Azure Defender for SQL should be enabled for unprotected PostgreSQL flexible servers
d38668f5-d155-42c7-ab3d-9b57b50f8fbf.d: Audit PostgreSQL flexible servers without Advanced Data Security

abda6d70-9778-44e7-84a8-06713e6db027.n: Azure SQL logical servers should have Microsoft Entra-only authentication enabled during creation
abda6d70-9778-44e7-84a8-06713e6db027.d: Require Azure SQL logical servers to be created with Microsoft Entra-only authentication. This policy doesn't block local authentication from being re-enabled on resources after create. Consider using the 'Microsoft Entra-only authentication' initiative instead to require both. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/adonlycreate.

090c7b07-b4ed-4561-ad20-e9075f3ccaff.n: Azure registry container images should have vulnerabilities resolved (powered by Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management)
090c7b07-b4ed-4561-ad20-e9075f3ccaff.d: Container image vulnerability assessment scans your registry for commonly known vulnerabilities (CVEs) and provides a detailed vulnerability report for each image. Resolving vulnerabilities can greatly improve your security posture, ensuring images are safe to use prior to deployment.

17f4b1cc-c55c-4d94-b1f9-2978f6ac2957.n: Azure running container images should have vulnerabilities resolved (powered by Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management)
17f4b1cc-c55c-4d94-b1f9-2978f6ac2957.d: Container image vulnerability assessment scans your registry for commonly known vulnerabilities (CVEs) and provides a detailed vulnerability report for each image. This recommendation provides visibility to vulnerable images currently running in your Kubernetes clusters. Remediating vulnerabilities in container images that are currently running is key to improving your security posture, significan

b954148f-4c11-4c38-8221-be76711e194a.n: An activity log alert should exist for specific Administrative operations
b954148f-4c11-4c38-8221-be76711e194a.d: This policy audits specific Administrative operations with no activity log alerts configured.

3ff60f98-7fa4-410a-9f7f-0b00f5afdbdd.n: Windows machines should meet requirements for 'Security Options - Network Access'
3ff60f98-7fa4-410a-9f7f-0b00f5afdbdd.d: Windows machines should have the specified Group Policy settings in the category 'Security Options - Network Access' for including access for anonymous users, local accounts, and remote access to the registry. This policy requires that the Guest Configuration prerequisites have been deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol.

0fea8f8a-4169-495d-8307-30ec335f387d.n: CORS should not allow every domain to access your API for FHIR
0fea8f8a-4169-495d-8307-30ec335f387d.d: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) should not allow all domains to access your API for FHIR. To protect your API for FHIR, remove access for all domains and explicitly define the domains allowed to connect.

f110a506-2dcb-422e-bcea-d533fc8c35e2.n: Azure Machine Learning compute instances should be recreated to get the latest software updates
f110a506-2dcb-422e-bcea-d533fc8c35e2.d: Ensure Azure Machine Learning compute instances run on the latest available operating system. Security is improved and vulnerabilities reduced by running with the latest security patches. For more information, visit https://aka.ms/azureml-ci-updates/.

bfecdea6-31c4-4045-ad42-71b9dc87247d.n: Storage account encryption scopes should use double encryption for data at rest
bfecdea6-31c4-4045-ad42-71b9dc87247d.d: Enable infrastructure encryption for encryption at rest of your storage account encryption scopes for added security. Infrastructure encryption ensures that your data is encrypted twice.

e0a2b1a3-f7f9-4569-807f-2a9edebdf4d9.n: Cosmos DB should use a virtual network service endpoint
e0a2b1a3-f7f9-4569-807f-2a9edebdf4d9.d: This policy audits any Cosmos DB not configured to use a virtual network service endpoint.

ee984370-154a-4ee8-9726-19d900e56fc0.n: Windows machines should meet requirements for 'Security Options - Accounts'
ee984370-154a-4ee8-9726-19d900e56fc0.d: Windows machines should have the specified Group Policy settings in the category 'Security Options - Accounts' for limiting local account use of blank passwords and guest account status. This policy requires that the Guest Configuration prerequisites have been deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol.

1f90fc71-a595-4066-8974-d4d0802e8ef0.n: Microsoft Defender CSPM should be enabled
1f90fc71-a595-4066-8974-d4d0802e8ef0.d: Defender Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) provides enhanced posture capabilities and a new intelligent cloud security graph to help identify, prioritize, and reduce risk. Defender CSPM is available in addition to the free foundational security posture capabilities turned on by default in Defender for Cloud.

f85bf3e0-d513-442e-89c3-1784ad63382b.n: System updates should be installed on your machines (powered by Update Center)
f85bf3e0-d513-442e-89c3-1784ad63382b.d: Your machines are missing system, security, and critical updates. Software updates often include critical patches to security holes. Such holes are frequently exploited in malware attacks so it's vital to keep your software updated. To install all outstanding patches and secure your machines, follow the remediation steps.

78215662-041e-49ed-a9dd-5385911b3a1f.n: Azure SQL Managed Instances should have Microsoft Entra-only authentication enabled during creation
78215662-041e-49ed-a9dd-5385911b3a1f.d: Require Azure SQL Managed Instance to be created with Microsoft Entra-only authentication. This policy doesn't block local authentication from being re-enabled on resources after create. Consider using the 'Microsoft Entra-only authentication' initiative instead to require both. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/adonlycreate.

df73bd95-24da-4a4f-96b9-4e8b94b402bd.n: API Management should disable public network access to the service configuration endpoints
df73bd95-24da-4a4f-96b9-4e8b94b402bd.d: To improve the security of API Management services, restrict connectivity to service configuration endpoints, like direct access management API, Git configuration management endpoint, or self-hosted gateways configuration endpoint.

d550e854-df1a-4de9-bf44-cd894b39a95e.n: Azure Monitor Logs for Application Insights should be linked to a Log Analytics workspace
d550e854-df1a-4de9-bf44-cd894b39a95e.d: Link the Application Insights component to a Log Analytics workspace for logs encryption. Customer-managed keys are commonly required to meet regulatory compliance and for more control over the access to your data in Azure Monitor. Linking your component to a Log Analytics workspace that's enabled with a customer-managed key, ensures that your Application Insights logs meet this compliance require

1dc2fc00-2245-4143-99f4-874c937f13ef.n: Azure API Management platform version should be stv2
1dc2fc00-2245-4143-99f4-874c937f13ef.d: Azure API Management stv1 compute platform version will be retired effective 31 August 2024, and these instances should be migrated to stv2 compute platform for continued support. Learn more at https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/api-management/breaking-changes/stv1-platform-retirement-august-2024

672fe5a1-2fcd-42d7-b85d-902b6e28c6ff.n: Guest Attestation extension should be installed on supported Linux virtual machines
672fe5a1-2fcd-42d7-b85d-902b6e28c6ff.d: Install Guest Attestation extension on supported Linux virtual machines to allow Azure Security Center to proactively attest and monitor the boot integrity. Once installed, boot integrity will be attested via Remote Attestation. This assessment applies to Trusted Launch and Confidential Linux virtual machines.

5d4e3c65-4873-47be-94f3-6f8b953a3598.n: Azure Event Hub namespaces should have local authentication methods disabled
5d4e3c65-4873-47be-94f3-6f8b953a3598.d: Disabling local authentication methods improves security by ensuring that Azure Event Hub namespaces exclusively require Microsoft Entra ID identities for authentication. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/disablelocalauth-eh.

6c53d030-cc64-46f0-906d-2bc061cd1334.n: Log Analytics workspaces should block log ingestion and querying from public networks
6c53d030-cc64-46f0-906d-2bc061cd1334.d: Improve workspace security by blocking log ingestion and querying from public networks. Only private-link connected networks will be able to ingest and query logs on this workspace. Learn more at https://aka.ms/AzMonPrivateLink#configure-log-analytics.

8405fdab-1faf-48aa-b702-999c9c172094.n: Managed disks should disable public network access
8405fdab-1faf-48aa-b702-999c9c172094.d: Disabling public network access improves security by ensuring that a managed disk isn't exposed on the public internet. Creating private endpoints can limit exposure of managed disks. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/disksprivatelinksdoc.

21a6bc25-125e-4d13-b82d-2e19b7208ab7.n: VPN gateways should use only Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) authentication for point-to-site users
21a6bc25-125e-4d13-b82d-2e19b7208ab7.d: Disabling local authentication methods improves security by ensuring that VPN Gateways use only Azure Active Directory identities for authentication. Learn more about Azure AD authentication at https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/vpn-gateway/openvpn-azure-ad-tenant

1bc02227-0cb6-4e11-8f53-eb0b22eab7e8.n: Application Insights components should block log ingestion and querying from public networks
1bc02227-0cb6-4e11-8f53-eb0b22eab7e8.d: Improve Application Insights security by blocking log ingestion and querying from public networks. Only private-link connected networks will be able to ingest and query logs of this component. Learn more at https://aka.ms/AzMonPrivateLink#configure-application-insights.

56fd377d-098c-4f02-8406-81eb055902b8.n: IP firewall rules on Azure Synapse workspaces should be removed
56fd377d-098c-4f02-8406-81eb055902b8.d: Removing all IP firewall rules improves security by ensuring your Azure Synapse workspace can only be accessed from a private endpoint. This configuration audits creation of firewall rules that allow public network access on the workspace.

deeddb44-9f94-4903-9fa0-081d524406e3.n: Azure Recovery Services vaults should use private link for backup
deeddb44-9f94-4903-9fa0-081d524406e3.d: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The Private Link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. By mapping private endpoints to Azure Recovery Services vaults, data leakage risks are reduced. Learn more about private links at: https://aka.ms/AB-

9f061a12-e40d-4183-a00e-171812443373.n: Kubernetes clusters should not use the default namespace
9f061a12-e40d-4183-a00e-171812443373.d: Prevent usage of the default namespace in Kubernetes clusters to protect against unauthorized access for ConfigMap, Pod, Secret, Service, and ServiceAccount resource types. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

f0308946-498a-43fd-8d44-a75b47cd2aef.n: Storage accounts should restrict network access (excluding storage accounts managed by Azure Red Hat OpenShift)
f0308946-498a-43fd-8d44-a75b47cd2aef.d: Network access to storage accounts should be restricted. Configure network rules so only applications from allowed networks can access the storage account. To allow connections from specific internet or on-premises clients, access can be granted to traffic from specific Azure virtual networks or to public internet IP address ranges. Storage accounts in resource groups managed by Azure Red Hat Open

c6283572-73bb-4deb-bf2c-7a2b8f7462cb.n: SQL server-targeted autoprovisioning should be enabled for SQL servers on machines plan
c6283572-73bb-4deb-bf2c-7a2b8f7462cb.d: To ensure your SQL VMs and Arc-enabled SQL Servers are protected, ensure the SQL-targeted Azure Monitoring Agent is configured to automatically deploy. This is also necessary if you've previously configured autoprovisioning of the Microsoft Monitoring Agent, as that component is being deprecated. Learn more: https://aka.ms/SQLAMAMigration

f5c8be13-ecfa-4ed7-beee-fcd8a6d9519d.n: Storage accounts should use customer-managed key for encryption (excluding storage accounts managed by Azure Red Hat OpenShift)
f5c8be13-ecfa-4ed7-beee-fcd8a6d9519d.d: Secure your blob and file storage account with greater flexibility using customer-managed keys. When you specify a customer-managed key, that key is used to protect and control access to the key that encrypts your data. Using customer-managed keys provides additional capabilities to control rotation of the key encryption key or cryptographically erase data. Storage accounts in resource groups mana

ed9bd083-7bfb-4fec-bbb4-12635e096a09.n: Storage accounts should restrict network access using virtual network rules (excluding storage accounts managed by ARO)
ed9bd083-7bfb-4fec-bbb4-12635e096a09.d: Protect your storage accounts from potential threats using virtual network rules as a preferred method instead of IP-based filtering. Disabling IP-based filtering prevents public IPs from accessing your storage accounts. Storage accounts in resource groups managed by Azure Red Hat OpenShift are excluded from evaluation.

db4f9b05-5ffd-4b34-b714-3c710dbb3fd6.n: Storage accounts should restrict network access using virtual network rules (excluding storage accounts created by Databricks)
db4f9b05-5ffd-4b34-b714-3c710dbb3fd6.d: Protect your storage accounts from potential threats using virtual network rules as a preferred method instead of IP-based filtering. Disabling IP-based filtering prevents public IPs from accessing your storage accounts.

18ac0011-fb88-42b6-a025-b33b6f0d2cb3.n: Storage accounts should use private link (excluding storage accounts managed by Azure Red Hat OpenShift)
18ac0011-fb88-42b6-a025-b33b6f0d2cb3.d: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The Private Link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. By mapping private endpoints to your storage account, data leakage risks are reduced. Learn more about private links at - https://aka.ms/azureprivate

1604f626-4d8d-4124-8bb8-b1e5f95562de.n: Storage accounts should use private link (excluding storage accounts created by Databricks)
1604f626-4d8d-4124-8bb8-b1e5f95562de.d: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The Private Link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. By mapping private endpoints to your storage account, data leakage risks are reduced. Learn more about private links at - https://aka.ms/azureprivate

1b4d1c4e-934c-4703-944c-27c82c06bebb.n: Diagnostic logs in Azure AI services resources should be enabled
1b4d1c4e-934c-4703-944c-27c82c06bebb.d: Enable logs for Azure AI services resources. This enables you to recreate activity trails for investigation purposes, when a security incident occurs or your network is compromised

138ff14d-b687-4faa-a81c-898c91a87fa2.n: Resource logs in Azure Databricks Workspaces should be enabled
138ff14d-b687-4faa-a81c-898c91a87fa2.d: Resource logs enable recreating activity trails to use for investigation purposes when a security incident occurs or when your network is compromised.

0e7849de-b939-4c50-ab48-fc6b0f5eeba2.n: Azure Databricks Workspaces should disable public network access
0e7849de-b939-4c50-ab48-fc6b0f5eeba2.d: Disabling public network access improves security by ensuring that the resource isn't exposed on the public internet. You can control exposure of your resources by creating private endpoints instead. Learn more at: https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/databricks/administration-guide/cloud-configurations/azure/private-link.

51c1490f-3319-459c-bbbc-7f391bbed753.n: Azure Databricks Clusters should disable public IP
51c1490f-3319-459c-bbbc-7f391bbed753.d: Disabling public IP of clusters in Azure Databricks Workspaces improves security by ensuring that the clusters aren't exposed on the public internet. Learn more at: https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/databricks/security/secure-cluster-connectivity.

9c25c9e4-ee12-4882-afd2-11fb9d87893f.n: Azure Databricks Workspaces should be in a virtual network
9c25c9e4-ee12-4882-afd2-11fb9d87893f.d: Azure Virtual Networks provide enhanced security and isolation for your Azure Databricks Workspaces, as well as subnets, access control policies, and other features to further restrict access. Learn more at: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/databricks/administration-guide/cloud-configurations/azure/vnet-inject.

258823f2-4595-4b52-b333-cc96192710d8.n: Azure Databricks Workspaces should use private link
258823f2-4595-4b52-b333-cc96192710d8.d: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual networks to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The Private Link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. By mapping private endpoints to Azure Databricks workspaces, you can reduce data leakage risks. Learn more about private links at: https://aka.ms/ad

b3a22bc9-66de-45fb-98fa-00f5df42f41a.n: Azure SQL Database should have Microsoft Entra-only authentication enabled
b3a22bc9-66de-45fb-98fa-00f5df42f41a.d: Require Azure SQL logical servers to use Microsoft Entra-only authentication. This policy doesn't block servers from being created with local authentication enabled. It does block local authentication from being enabled on resources after create. Consider using the 'Microsoft Entra-only authentication' initiative instead to require both. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/adonlycreate.

0c28c3fb-c244-42d5-a9bf-f35f2999577b.n: Azure SQL Managed Instance should have Microsoft Entra-only authentication enabled
0c28c3fb-c244-42d5-a9bf-f35f2999577b.d: Require Azure SQL Managed Instance to use Microsoft Entra-only authentication. This policy doesn't block Azure SQL Managed instances from being created with local authentication enabled. It does block local authentication from being enabled on resources after create. Consider using the 'Microsoft Entra-only authentication' initiative instead to require both. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/adonlycre

6ea81a52-5ca7-4575-9669-eaa910b7edf8.n: Synapse Workspaces should have Microsoft Entra-only authentication enabled
6ea81a52-5ca7-4575-9669-eaa910b7edf8.d: Require Synapse Workspaces to use Microsoft Entra-only authentication. This policy doesn't block workspaces from being created with local authentication enabled. It does block local authentication from being enabled on resources after create. Consider using the 'Microsoft Entra-only authentication' initiative instead to require both. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/Synapse.

3aa03346-d8c5-4994-a5bc-7652c2a2aef1.n: API Management subscriptions should not be scoped to all APIs
3aa03346-d8c5-4994-a5bc-7652c2a2aef1.d: API Management subscriptions should be scoped to a product or an individual API instead of all APIs, which could result in an excessive data exposure.

92bb331d-ac71-416a-8c91-02f2cb734ce4.n: API Management calls to API backends should not bypass certificate thumbprint or name validation
92bb331d-ac71-416a-8c91-02f2cb734ce4.d: To improve the API security, API Management should validate the backend server certificate for all API calls. Enable SSL certificate thumbprint and name validation.

ee7495e7-3ba7-40b6-bfee-c29e22cc75d4.n: API Management APIs should use only encrypted protocols
ee7495e7-3ba7-40b6-bfee-c29e22cc75d4.d: To ensure security of data in transit, APIs should be available only through encrypted protocols, like HTTPS or WSS. Avoid using unsecured protocols, such as HTTP or WS.

f1cc7827-022c-473e-836e-5a51cae0b249.n: API Management secret named values should be stored in Azure Key Vault
f1cc7827-022c-473e-836e-5a51cae0b249.d: Named values are a collection of name and value pairs in each API Management service. Secret values can be stored either as encrypted text in API Management (custom secrets) or by referencing secrets in Azure Key Vault. To improve security of API Management and secrets, reference secret named values from Azure Key Vault. Azure Key Vault supports granular access management and secret rotation polic

b741306c-968e-4b67-b916-5675e5c709f4.n: API Management direct management endpoint should not be enabled
b741306c-968e-4b67-b916-5675e5c709f4.d: The direct management REST API in Azure API Management bypasses Azure Resource Manager role-based access control, authorization, and throttling mechanisms, thus increasing the vulnerability of your service.

c15dcc82-b93c-4dcb-9332-fbf121685b54.n: API Management calls to API backends should be authenticated
c15dcc82-b93c-4dcb-9332-fbf121685b54.d: Calls from API Management to backends should use some form of authentication, whether via certificates or credentials. Does not apply to Service Fabric backends.

c8acafaf-3d23-44d1-9624-978ef0f8652c.n: API endpoints that are unused should be disabled and removed from the Azure API Management service
c8acafaf-3d23-44d1-9624-978ef0f8652c.d: As a security best practice, API endpoints that haven't received traffic for 30 days are considered unused and should be removed from the Azure API Management service. Keeping unused API endpoints may pose a security risk to your organization. These may be APIs that should have been deprecated from the Azure API Management service but may have been accidentally left active. Such APIs typically do

05f95bb8-8ef8-4cef-8cad-5d30f9912850.n: Storage accounts should prevent shared key access (excluding storage accounts managed by Azure Red Hat OpenShift)
05f95bb8-8ef8-4cef-8cad-5d30f9912850.d: Audit requirement of Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) to authorize requests for your storage account. By default, requests can be authorized with either Azure Active Directory credentials, or by using the account access key for Shared Key authorization. Of these two types of authorization, Azure AD provides superior security and ease of use over Shared Key, and is recommended by Microsoft. Storag

fd9903f1-38c2-4d36-8e44-5c1c20c561e8.n: Storage accounts should prevent shared key access (excluding storage accounts created by Databricks)
fd9903f1-38c2-4d36-8e44-5c1c20c561e8.d: Audit requirement of Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) to authorize requests for your storage account. By default, requests can be authorized with either Azure Active Directory credentials, or by using the account access key for Shared Key authorization. Of these two types of authorization, Azure AD provides superior security and ease of use over Shared Key, and is recommended by Microsoft.

5e6bf724-0154-49bc-985f-27b2e07e636b.n: [Preview]: Azure Stack HCI servers should meet Secured-core requirements
5e6bf724-0154-49bc-985f-27b2e07e636b.d: Ensure that all Azure Stack HCI servers meet the Secured-core requirements. To enable the Secured-core server requirements: 1. From the Azure Stack HCI clusters page, go to Windows Admin Center and select Connect. 2. Go to the Security extension and select Secured-core. 3. Select any setting that is not enabled and click Enable.

dad3a6b9-4451-492f-a95c-69efc6f3fada.n: [Preview]: Azure Stack HCI servers should have consistently enforced application control policies
dad3a6b9-4451-492f-a95c-69efc6f3fada.d: At a minimum, apply the Microsoft WDAC base policy in enforced mode on all Azure Stack HCI servers. Applied Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) policies must be consistent across servers in the same cluster.

ee8ca833-1583-4d24-837e-96c2af9488a4.n: [Preview]: Azure Stack HCI systems should have encrypted volumes
ee8ca833-1583-4d24-837e-96c2af9488a4.d: Use BitLocker to encrypt the OS and data volumes on Azure Stack HCI systems.

36f0d6bc-a253-4df8-b25b-c3a5023ff443.n: [Preview]: Host and VM networking should be protected on Azure Stack HCI systems
36f0d6bc-a253-4df8-b25b-c3a5023ff443.d: Protect data on the Azure Stack HCI hosts network and on virtual machine network connections.

fe83a0eb-a853-422d-aac2-1bffd182c5d0.n: Storage accounts should have the specified minimum TLS version
fe83a0eb-a853-422d-aac2-1bffd182c5d0.d: Configure a minimum TLS version for secure communication between the client application and the storage account. To minimize security risk, the recommended minimum TLS version is the latest released version, which is currently TLS 1.2.

eb6f77b9-bd53-4e35-a23d-7f65d5f0e43d.n: Log checkpoints should be enabled for PostgreSQL database servers
eb6f77b9-bd53-4e35-a23d-7f65d5f0e43d.d: This policy helps audit any PostgreSQL databases in your environment without log_checkpoints setting enabled.

eb6f77b9-bd53-4e35-a23d-7f65d5f0e442.n: Log connections should be enabled for PostgreSQL database servers
eb6f77b9-bd53-4e35-a23d-7f65d5f0e442.d: This policy helps audit any PostgreSQL databases in your environment without log_connections setting enabled.

eb6f77b9-bd53-4e35-a23d-7f65d5f0e446.n: Disconnections should be logged for PostgreSQL database servers.
eb6f77b9-bd53-4e35-a23d-7f65d5f0e446.d: This policy helps audit any PostgreSQL databases in your environment without log_disconnections enabled.

5345bb39-67dc-4960-a1bf-427e16b9a0bd.n: Connection throttling should be enabled for PostgreSQL database servers
5345bb39-67dc-4960-a1bf-427e16b9a0bd.d: This policy helps audit any PostgreSQL databases in your environment without Connection throttling enabled. This setting enables temporary connection throttling per IP for too many invalid password login failures.

fbb99e8e-e444-4da0-9ff1-75c92f5a85b2.n: Storage account containing the container with activity logs must be encrypted with BYOK
fbb99e8e-e444-4da0-9ff1-75c92f5a85b2.d: This policy audits if the Storage account containing the container with activity logs is encrypted with BYOK. The policy works only if the storage account lies on the same subscription as activity logs by design. More information on Azure Storage encryption at rest can be found here https://aka.ms/azurestoragebyok.

27960feb-a23c-4577-8d36-ef8b5f35e0be.n: All flow log resources should be in enabled state
27960feb-a23c-4577-8d36-ef8b5f35e0be.d: Audit for flow log resources to verify if flow log status is enabled. Enabling flow logs allows to log information about IP traffic flowing. It can be used for optimizing network flows, monitoring throughput, verifying compliance, detecting intrusions and more.

c0e996f8-39cf-4af9-9f45-83fbde810432.n: Only approved VM extensions should be installed
c0e996f8-39cf-4af9-9f45-83fbde810432.d: This policy governs the virtual machine extensions that are not approved.

f466b2a6-823d-470d-8ea5-b031e72d79ae.n: App Service app slots that use PHP should use a specified 'PHP version'
f466b2a6-823d-470d-8ea5-b031e72d79ae.d: Periodically, newer versions are released for PHP software either due to security flaws or to include additional functionality. Using the latest PHP version for App Service apps is recommended in order to take advantage of security fixes, if any, and/or new functionalities of the latest version. 1760f9d4-7206-436e-a28f-d9f3a5c8a227.n: Azure Batch pools should have disk encryption enabled
1760f9d4-7206-436e-a28f-d9f3a5c8a227.d: Enabling Azure Batch disk encryption ensures that data is always encrypted at rest on your Azure Batch compute node. Learn more about disk encryption in Batch at https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/batch/disk-encryption.

09aa11bb-87ec-409f-bf0b-49b7c1561a87.d: Use customer-managed keys (CMK) to manage the encryption at rest of your on-disk data. You are able to select the allowed encrypted sets and all others are rejected when attached to a disk. Learn more at https://aka.ms/disks-cmk.

a22065a3-3b04-46ff-b84c-2d30e5c300d0.n: Azure Virtual Desktop hostpools should disable public network access only on session hosts
a22065a3-3b04-46ff-b84c-2d30e5c300d0.d: Disabling public network access for your Azure Virtual Desktop hostpool session hosts, but allowing public access for end users improves security by limiting exposure to the public internet. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/avdprivatelink.

6a92fe1f-0b86-44ae-843d-2db3d2b571ae.n: ElasticSan should disable public network access
6a92fe1f-0b86-44ae-843d-2db3d2b571ae.d: Disable public network access for your ElasticSan so that it's not accessible over the public internet. This can reduce data leakage risks.

7698f4ed-80ce-4e13-b408-ee135fa400a5.n: ElasticSan Volume Group should use customer-managed keys to encrypt data at rest
7698f4ed-80ce-4e13-b408-ee135fa400a5.d: Use customer-managed keys to manage the encryption at rest of your VolumeGroup. 67dcad1a-ec60-45df-8fd0-14c9d29eeaa2.n: Azure Event Grid namespaces should disable public network access
67dcad1a-ec60-45df-8fd0-14c9d29eeaa2.d: Disabling public network access improves security by ensuring that the resource isn't exposed on the public internet. You can limit exposure of your resources by creating private endpoints instead. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/aeg-ns-privateendpoints.

836cd60e-87f3-4e6a-a27c-29d687f01a4c.d: Enabling double encryption helps protect and safeguard your data to meet your organizational security and compliance commitments. When double encryption has been enabled, data in the storage account is encrypted twice, once at the service level and once at the infrastructure level, using two different encryption algorithms and two different keys.

43c323f6-0329-4f7c-a19a-6e5a5690d042.d: Encryption of data at rest in Azure Device Update with customer-managed key adds a second layer of encryption on top of the default service-managed keys, enables customer control of keys, custom rotation policies, and ability to manage access to data through key access control. 12c74c95-0efd-48da-b8d9-2a7d68470c92.d: Use customer-managed keys to manage the encryption at rest of your PostgreSQL flexible servers. 6599ab01-29bc-4852-a6f5-de9e2151714a.d: Enable transparent data encryption (TDE) at-rest on an Azure Arc-enabled SQL Managed Instance. Learn more at https://aka.ms/EnableTDEArcSQLMI.

ddcf4b94-9dfa-4a80-aca6-22bb654fde72.d: Disallow the creation of SMB Volumes without SMB3 encryption to ensure data integrity and data privacy.

7c6c7139-7d8e-45d0-9d94-72386a61308b.n: Azure NetApp Files Volumes of type NFSv4.1 should use Kerberos data encryption
7c6c7139-7d8e-45d0-9d94-72386a61308b.d: Only allow the use of Kerberos privacy (5p) security mode to ensure data is encrypted.

f0e5abd0-2554-4736-b7c0-4ffef23475ef.n: Queue Storage should use customer-managed key for encryption
f0e5abd0-2554-4736-b7c0-4ffef23475ef.d: Secure your queue storage with greater flexibility using customer-managed keys. When you specify a customer-managed key, that key is used to protect and control access to the key that encrypts your data. Using customer-managed keys provides additional capabilities to control rotation of the key encryption key or cryptographically erase data.

7c322315-e26d-4174-a99e-f49d351b4688.n: Table Storage should use customer-managed key for encryption
7c322315-e26d-4174-a99e-f49d351b4688.d: Secure your table storage with greater flexibility using customer-managed keys. 9798d31d-6028-4dee-8643-46102185c016.d: This policy audits if soft delete is enabled for Backup vaults in the scope. Soft delete can help you recover your data after it has been deleted. Learn more at https://aka.ms/AB-SoftDelete

deb528de-8f89-4101-881c-595899253102.n: Function app slots should use the latest TLS version
deb528de-8f89-4101-881c-595899253102.d: Periodically, newer versions are released for TLS either due to security flaws, include additional functionality, and enhance speed. Upgrade to the latest TLS version for Function apps to take advantage of security fixes, if any, and/or new functionalities of the latest version.

4ee5b817-627a-435a-8932-116193268172.n: App Service app slots should use the latest TLS version
4ee5b817-627a-435a-8932-116193268172.d: Periodically, newer versions are released for TLS either due to security flaws, include additional functionality, and enhance speed. Upgrade to the latest TLS version for App Service apps to take advantage of security fixes, if any, and/or new functionalities of the latest version.

817dcf37-e83d-4999-a472-644eada2ea1e.n: App Service Environment should be configured with strongest TLS Cipher suites
817dcf37-e83d-4999-a472-644eada2ea1e.d: The two most minimal and strongest cipher suites required for App Service Environment to function correctly are : TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 and TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256.

d6545c6b-dd9d-4265-91e6-0b451e2f1c50.n: App Service Environment should have TLS 1.0 and 1.1 disabled
d6545c6b-dd9d-4265-91e6-0b451e2f1c50.d: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are out-of-date protocols that do not support modern cryptographic algorithms. Disabling inbound TLS 1.0 and 1.1 traffic helps secure apps in an App Service Environment.

6164527b-e1ee-4882-8673-572f425f5e0a.n: Bot Service endpoint should be a valid HTTPS URI
6164527b-e1ee-4882-8673-572f425f5e0a.d: Data can be tampered with during transmission. Protocols exist that provide encryption to address problems of misuse and tampering. To ensure your bots are communicating only over encrypted channels, set the endpoint to a valid HTTPS URI. This ensures the HTTPS protocol is used to encrypt your data in transit and is also often a requirement for compliance with regulatory or industry standards. Ple

679da822-78a7-4eff-8fff-a899454a9970.n: Azure Front Door Standard and Premium should be running minimum TLS version of 1.2
679da822-78a7-4eff-8fff-a899454a9970.d: Setting minimal TLS version to 1.2 improves security by ensuring your custom domains are accessed from clients using TLS 1.2 or newer. Using versions of TLS less than 1.2 is not recommended since they are weak and do not support modern cryptographic algorithms.

49a22571-d204-4c91-a7b6-09b1a586fbc9.n: Keys should have the specified maximum validity period
49a22571-d204-4c91-a7b6-09b1a586fbc9.d: Manage your organizational compliance requirements by specifying the maximum amount of time in days that a key can be valid within your key vault.

c26e4b24-cf98-4c67-b48b-5a25c4c69eb9.n: Keys should not be active for longer than the specified number of days
c26e4b24-cf98-4c67-b48b-5a25c4c69eb9.d: Specify the number of days that a key should be active. Keys that are used for an extended period of time increase the probability that an attacker could compromise the key. As a good security practice, make sure that your keys have not been active longer than two years.

b0eb591a-5e70-4534-a8bf-04b9c489584a.n: Secrets should have more than the specified number of days before expiration
b0eb591a-5e70-4534-a8bf-04b9c489584a.d: If a secret is too close to expiration, an organizational delay to rotate the secret may result in an outage. Secrets should be rotated at a specified number of days prior to expiration to provide sufficient time to react to a failure.

342e8053-e12e-4c44-be01-c3c2f318400f.n: Secrets should have the specified maximum validity period
342e8053-e12e-4c44-be01-c3c2f318400f.d: Manage your organizational compliance requirements by specifying the maximum amount of time in days that a secret can be valid within your key vault.

e8d99835-8a06-45ae-a8e0-87a91941ccfe.n: Secrets should not be active for longer than the specified number of days
e8d99835-8a06-45ae-a8e0-87a91941ccfe.d: If your secrets were created with an activation date set in the future, you must ensure that your secrets have not been active for longer than the specified duration.

f772fb64-8e40-40ad-87bc-7706e1949427.n: Certificates should not expire within the specified number of days
f772fb64-8e40-40ad-87bc-7706e1949427.d: Manage certificates that will expire within a specified number of days to ensure your organization has sufficient time to rotate the certificate prior to expiration.

dc921057-6b28-4fbe-9b83-f7bec05db6c2.n: Container registries should have local admin account disabled.
dc921057-6b28-4fbe-9b83-f7bec05db6c2.d: Disable admin account for your registry so that it is not accessible by local admin. Disabling local authentication methods like admin user, repository scoped access tokens and anonymous pull improves security by ensuring that container registries exclusively require Azure Active Directory identities for authentication. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/acr/authentication.

199d5677-e4d9-4264-9465-efe1839c06bd.n: Application Insights components should block non-Azure Active Directory based ingestion.
199d5677-e4d9-4264-9465-efe1839c06bd.d: Enforcing log ingestion to require Azure Active Directory authentication prevents unauthenticated logs from an attacker which could lead to incorrect status, false alerts, and incorrect logs stored in the system.

4e6c27d5-a6ee-49cf-b2b4-d8fe90fa2b8b.n: Users must authenticate with multi-factor authentication to create or update resources
4e6c27d5-a6ee-49cf-b2b4-d8fe90fa2b8b.d: This policy definition blocks resource create and update operations when the caller is not authenticated via MFA. For more information, visit https://aka.ms/mfaforazure.

dea83a72-443c-4292-83d5-54a2f98749c0.n: Automation Account should have Managed Identity
dea83a72-443c-4292-83d5-54a2f98749c0.d: Use Managed Identities as the recommended method for authenticating with Azure resources from the runbooks. Managed identity for authentication is more secure and eliminates the management overhead associated with using RunAs Account in your runbook code .

fe3fd216-4f83-4fc1-8984-2bbec80a3418.n: Cognitive Services accounts should use a managed identity
fe3fd216-4f83-4fc1-8984-2bbec80a3418.d: Assigning a managed identity to your Cognitive Service account helps ensure secure authentication. This identity is used by this Cognitive service account to communicate with other Azure services, like Azure Key Vault, in a secure way without you having to manage any credentials.

5e7e928c-8693-4a23-9bf3-1c77b9a8fe97.d: To improve the security of Azure Attestation Service, ensure that it isn't exposed to the public internet and can only be accessed from a private endpoint. Disable the public network access property as described in aka.ms/azureattestation.
